arXiv:2403.01154v5 [math.AG] 19 Sep 2025

Boundedness of klt complements on Fano fibrations over surfaces

Bingyi Chen Address: Bingyi Chen, Department of Mathematics, Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, 510275, P. R. China. Email address: chenby253@mail.sysu.edu.cn, chenby16@tsinghua.org.cn
Abstract.

Let (X,B)(X,B) be an ϵ\epsilon-lc pair of dimension dd with a closed point x∈Xx\in X. Birkar and Shokurov conjectured that there is an effective Cartier divisor HH passing through xx such that (X,B+t​H)(X,B+tH) is lc near xx, where tt is a positive real number depending only on d,ϵd,\epsilon. We prove that this conjecture is equivalent to Shokurov’s conjecture on boundedness of klt complements on Fano fibrations and we confirm it in dimension 2. As a corollary, we prove the boundedness of klt complements on Fano fibrations over surfaces.

1. Introduction

We work over the field of complex numbers ℂ\mathbb{C}. All varieties are assumed to be quasi-projective.

The theory of complements was introduced by Shokurov when he investigated log flips on threefolds [Sh92], which turns out to be a very powerful tool in birational geometry. It has played an important role in several breakthroughs in birational geometry, for example, the proof of the Borisov-Alexeev-Borisov conjecture (the boundedness of Fano varieties) [Bi19, Bi21] and the openness of K-semistability in families of log Fano pairs [Xu20, BLX22]. See [Sh00, Sh04, Liu18, HLS19, Sh20, Bi22, HL22, HLL22, CHL23] for more applications.

Shokurov [Sh00, Sh04] proposed conjectures on the boundedness of lc (resp. klt) complements, i.e. the existence of lc (resp. klt) nn-complements for some bounded natural number nn. The boundedness of lc complements was proved by Birkar [Bi19] for pairs on Fano type fibrations with boundary coefficients in a hyperstandard set, which was later generalized to more general boundary coefficients [HLS19, Sh20]. On the other hand, the conjecture on the boundedness of klt complements is still wide open except some partial results (see Remark 1.2 below).

We now state precisely Shokurov’s conjecture on the boundedness of klt complements for the case when boundary coefficients belong to a finite set of rational numbers.

Conjecture 1.1 (Shokurov).

Let dd be a natural number, ϵ\epsilon be a positive real number and ℜ⊂[0,1]\mathfrak{R}\subset[0,1] be a finite set of rational numbers. Then there is a natural number nn depending only on d,ϵ,ℜd,\epsilon,\mathfrak{R} satisfying the following. Assume (X,B)(X,B) is a pair, X→ZX\to Z is a contraction and z∈Zz\in Z is a closed point such that

  • •

    (X,B)(X,B) is ϵ\epsilon-lc of dimension dd,

  • •

    the coefficients of BB are in ℜ\mathfrak{R},

  • •

    XX is of Fano type over ZZ, and

  • •

    −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ.

Then KX+BK_{X}+B has a monotonic klt nn-complement over zz. That is, there is a ℚ\mathbb{Q}-divisor Λ\Lambda on XX such that over some neighbourhood of zz we have

  • •

    Λ≥B\Lambda\geq B,

  • •

    (X,Λ)(X,\Lambda) is klt, and

  • •

    n⁡(KX+Λ)∼0/Zn(K_{X}+\Lambda)\sim 0/Z.

Remark 1.2

(1) It is expected that KX+BK_{X}+B has not just a klt nn-complement but also an ϵ\epsilon-lc nn-complement, even for more general boundary coefficients. See [Sh20, Conjecture 5] and [CH21, Conjecture 1.1] for stronger versions of Conjecture 1.1.

(2) The condition in Conjecture 1.1 that

  • •

    (X,B)(X,B) is ϵ\epsilon-lc and −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ,

can be replaced by another equivalent condition that

  • •

    KX+BK_{X}+B has an ϵ\epsilon-lc ℝ\mathbb{R}-complement over ZZ, that is, there is an ϵ\epsilon-lc pair (X,B+)(X,B^{+}) such that B+≥BB^{+}\geq B and KX+B+∼ℝ0/ZK_{X}+B^{+}\sim_{\mathbb{R}}0/Z.

Indeed, if the former holds, as XX is of Fano type over ZZ, −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is semiample over ZZ and hence the latter follows; if the latter holds, we can run an MMP on −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) over ZZ to make −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) nef over ZZ and in this process the ϵ\epsilon-lc property of (X,B)(X,B) will be preserved because of the existence of ϵ\epsilon-lc ℝ\mathbb{R}-complement.

(3) When dimZ=0\dim Z=0, Conjecture 1.1 is equivalent to the Borisov-Alexeev-Borisov conjecture [Bi19, Bi21].

(4) When dimZ=1\dim Z=1, Conjecture 1.1 was confirmed by Birkar [Bi23, Corollary 1.4].

(5) In the toric case, Conjecture 1.1 was proved by Ambro [Am22, Theorem 1.2].

(6) When dimX=2\dim X=2, an affirmative answer of Conjecture 1.1 was given in [Bi04, Theorem 1.6] and in [CH21, Theorem 1.1].

(7) When X=ZX=Z, dimX=3\dim X=3, ϵ≥1\epsilon\geq 1 and XX is terminal, Conjecture 1.1 was proved in [HLL22, Theorem 1.4].

(8) When X=ZX=Z and (X∋z,B)(X\ni z,B) has a δ\delta-plt blow-up (Definition 2.26) for some fixed δ>0\delta>0, Conjecture 1.1 follows from [HLS19, Theorem 1.6]. In particular, Conjecture 1.1 holds when X=ZX=Z and (X∋z,B)(X\ni z,B) is an exceptional singularity (see Definition 2.28).

(9) When (X,Γ)→Z(X,\Gamma)\to Z is a (d,r,ϵ)(d,r,\epsilon)-Fano type fibration (see [Bi22, Definition 1.1]) and B≤ΓB\leq\Gamma with −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) being big over ZZ, Conjecture 1.1 was proved in [Bi22, Theorem 1.7]. Roughly speaking, Conjecture 1.1 holds when ZZ belongs to a bounded family and the “degree” of KX+BK_{X}+B is in some sense bounded.

(10) When (X,B)→Z(X,B)\to Z is a semi-stable morphism ([FM18, 2.7]) and m​KZmK_{Z} is Cartier for some fixed mm, Conjecture 1.1 was proved in [FM18, Theorem 1.4].

To attack the above conjecture, Birkar and Shokurov proposed the following two conjectures. Birkar pointed out to me that these two conjectures are equivalent and can imply Conjecture 1.1.

Conjecture 1.3 (Birkar-Shokurov).

Let dd be a natural number and ϵ\epsilon be a positive real number. Then there is a positive real number tt depending only on d,ϵd,\epsilon satisfying the following. Assume (X,B)(X,B) is a pair, f:X→Zf:X\to Z is a contraction and z∈Zz\in Z is a closed point such that

  • •

    (X,B)(X,B) is ϵ\epsilon-lc of dimension dd and dimZ>0\dim Z>0,

  • •

    XX is of Fano type over ZZ, and

  • •

    −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ.

Then there exists an effective Cartier divisor HH on some neighbourhood UU of z∈Zz\in Z such that z∈Supp⁡Hz\in\Supp H and (X,B+t​f∗​H)(X,B+tf^{*}H) is lc over UU.

Conjecture 1.4 (Birkar-Shokurov).

Let ss be a natural number and ϵ\epsilon be a positive real number. Then there is a positive real number tt depending only on s,ϵs,\epsilon satisfying the following. Assume (Z,Δ)(Z,\Delta) is an ϵ\epsilon-lc pair of dimension ss with a closed point z∈Zz\in Z. Then there exists an effective Cartier divisor HH on some neighbourhood of z∈Zz\in Z such that z∈Supp⁡Hz\in\Supp H and (Z,Δ+t​H)(Z,\Delta+tH) is lc near zz.

Remark 1.5

(1) Conjecture 1.4 is a special case of Conjecture 1.3 when X=ZX=Z.

(2) As in Remark 1.2(2), in Conjecture 1.3 the condition that (X,B)(X,B) is ϵ\epsilon-lc and −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ can be replaced by another equivalent condition that KX+BK_{X}+B has an ϵ\epsilon-lc ℝ\mathbb{R}-complement over ZZ.

(3) At a meeting of the COW seminar at City, University of London on 7th February 2018, Birkar raised Conjecture 1.3 in the special case when Z=𝔸nZ=\mathbb{A}^{n}, X→ZX\to Z is a weighted blow up at the origin and B=0B=0 (see [SS21, Conjecture 1.2]). It was proved by G. Sankaran and F. Santos in [SS21, Theorem 1.3] that Conjecture 1.3 holds in this case.

(4) Ambro had independently considered a version of these conjectures in private work. He [Am22, Theorem 3.12] proved Conjecture 1.3 in the toric setting with an additional condition that the coefficients of BB belong to a fixed DCC set.

(5) When dimZ=1\dim Z=1, Conjecture 1.3 was proved by Birkar in [Bi23, Theorem 1.1]. See [Bi16, Theorem 1.4] for another proof of Conjecture 1.3 in the special case when dimZ=1\dim Z=1, KX+B∼ℝ0/ZK_{X}+B\sim_{\mathbb{R}}0/Z and (F,Supp⁡B|F)(F,\Supp B|_{F}) is log bounded where FF is a general fiber of ff.

Relations among the above conjectures. Our first main result is on the relations among Conjecture 1.1, 1.3 and 1.4.

Theorem 1.6.

Let ℓ\ell be a natural number. The following are equivalent:

  1. (1)

    Conjecture 1.1 holds when dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell;

  2. (2)

    Conjecture 1.1 holds when X→ZX\to Z is birational, B=0B=0 and dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell.

  3. (3)

    Conjecture 1.3 holds when dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell.

  4. (4)

    Conjecture 1.3 holds when X→ZX\to Z is birational, B=0B=0 and dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell.

  5. (5)

    Conjecture 1.4 holds when dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell.

It is worth to mention that the proof of the above theorem relies on [Bi23, Theorem 1.1], which relates the singularities on the base space of a Fano type fibration with the singularities on the total space.

The surface case. We confirm Conjecture 1.4 in dimension 2. As a corollary, we prove the boundedness of klt complements on Fano fibrations over surfaces.

Theorem 1.7.

Let (Z,Δ)(Z,\Delta) be a pair of dimension 2 with a closed point z∈Zz\in Z such that mld⁡(Z∋z,Δ)≥ϵ\mld(Z\ni z,\Delta)\geq\epsilon with 0<ϵ≤10<\epsilon\leq 1. Then there exists an effective Cartier divisor HH on some neighbourhood of z∈Zz\in Z such that z∈Supp⁡Hz\in\Supp H and (Z,Δ+t​H)(Z,\Delta+tH) is lc near zz, where t=ϵ2/24t=\epsilon^{2}/24.

Here we denote by mld⁡(Z∋z,Δ)\mld(Z\ni z,\Delta) the infimum of the log discrepancy of EE with respect to (Z,Δ)(Z,\Delta) where EE runs over all prime divisors over ZZ with centerZ⁡E=z\cent_{Z}E=z. Note that the condition mld⁡(Z∋z,Δ)≥ϵ\mld(Z\ni z,\Delta)\geq\epsilon is weaker than that (Z,Δ)(Z,\Delta) is ϵ\epsilon-lc near zz.

Corollary 1.8.

Conjecture 1.1, 1.3 and 1.4 hold when dimZ≤2\dim Z\leq 2.

Remark 1.9

The following example indicates that the order O⁡(ϵ2)O(\epsilon^{2}) in Theorem 1.7 is optimal.

Example 1.10

Let Z=𝔸2Z=\mathbb{A}^{2} with coordinates x,yx,y and let z∈Zz\in Z be the origin. Let

Δ=2​m−1m2⋅(xm+ym+1=0)\Delta=\frac{2m-1}{m^{2}}\cdot(x^{m}+y^{m+1}=0)

where m∈ℕm\in\mathbb{N}. By [Ch22, Lemma A.1] we have

mld⁡(Z∋z,Δ)=inf{p1+p2−min⁡{λ​m​p1,λ⁡(m+1)​p2}∣(p1,p2)∈ℕ2}\mld(Z\ni z,\Delta)=\inf\{p_{1}+p_{2}-\min\{\lambda mp_{1},\lambda(m+1)p_{2}\}\mid(p_{1},p_{2})\in\mathbb{N}^{2}\}

where λ=2​m−1m2\lambda=\frac{2m-1}{m^{2}}. It is not hard to check that the above expression is equal to 1m\frac{1}{m}. So we have

mld⁡(Z∋z,Δ)=1m.\mld(Z\ni z,\Delta)=\frac{1}{m}.

Let EE be the exceptional divisor obtained by the weighted blow up at zz with wt​(x,y)=(m+1,m)\textbf{wt}(x,y)=(m+1,m). Then a⁡(E,Z,Δ)=1ma(E,Z,\Delta)=\frac{1}{m}. Moreover, the vanishing order of the pullback of xx (resp. yy) along EE is m+1m+1 (resp. mm). So for any curve HH on ZZ passing through zz, (Z,Δ+t​H)(Z,\Delta+tH) is not lc near zz when t>1m2t>\frac{1}{m^{2}}.

The toric case. As mentioned in Remark 1.5, in the toric case Conjecture 1.3 was proved by Ambro [Am22, Theorem 3.12] with an additional condition that the coefficients of BB belong to a fixed DCC set. In the following theorem we remove this additional condition.

Theorem 1.11.

Conjecture 1.3 holds when f:X→Zf:X\to Z is a toric contraction between toric varieties, (X,B)(X,B) is a toric pair and z∈Zz\in Z is a torus invariant closed point.

Corollary 1.12.

Conjecture 1.4 holds when (Z,Δ)(Z,\Delta) is a toric pair and z∈Zz\in Z is a torus invariant closed point.

Remark 1.13

(1) See Theorem 8.3 for a stronger version of Theorem 1.11, which asserts that Conjecture 1.3 holds in the toric case, even when we replace the condition that (X,B)(X,B) is ϵ\epsilon-lc by a weaker condition that mld(X/Z∋z,B)≥ϵ\mld(X/Z\ni z,B)\geq\epsilon, that is, a⁡(E,X,B)≥ϵa(E,X,B)\geq\epsilon for any prime divisor EE over XX with f⁡(centerX⁡E)=zf(\cent_{X}E)=z.

(2) After this paper was completed, Ambro informed me that he had proved Theorem 1.11 with an effective estimate for tt (under the weaker condition that mld(X/Z∋z,B)≥ϵ\mld(X/Z\ni z,B)\geq\epsilon).

The case for exceptional singularities. We confirm Conjecture 1.4 for singularities admitting δ\delta-plt blow-ups (Definition 2.26) for some fixed δ>0\delta>0. As a corollary, we prove the boundedness of klt complements over an exceptional singularity (Definition 2.28) Z∋zZ\ni z of dimension 3.

Theorem 1.14.

Fix a positive real number δ\delta. Conjecture 1.4 holds when (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) has a δ\delta-plt blow-up.

Theorem 1.15.

Fix a DCC set 𝔇⊂[0,1]\mathfrak{D}\subset[0,1]. Conjecture 1.4 holds when there is a boundary Ω\Omega on ZZ such that

  • •

    Ω≤Δ\Omega\leq\Delta,

  • •

    (Z∋z,Ω)(Z\ni z,\Omega) is an exceptional singularity, and

  • •

    the coefficients of Ω\Omega are in 𝔇\mathfrak{D}.

Corollary 1.16.

Conjecture 1.3 and 1.4 hold when Z∋zZ\ni z is an exceptional singularity.

Corollary 1.17.

Conjecture 1.1 holds when Z∋zZ\ni z is an exceptional singularity and dimZ=3\dim Z=3.

2. Preliminaries

We will freely use the standard notations and definitions in [KM98, BCHM]. A contraction f:X→Zf:X\rightarrow Z is a projective morphism of normal varieties with f∗​𝒪X=𝒪Zf_{*}\mathcal{O}_{X}=\mathcal{O}_{Z}.

2.1. Divisors and ideals

Let XX be a normal variety, DD be an ℝ\mathbb{R}-divisor on XX and 𝔞\mathfrak{a} be a non-zero ideal sheaf on XX. For a prime divisor TT on XX, we denote by μT​D\mu_{T}D the coefficient of TT in DD and denote by μT​𝔞\mu_{T}\mathfrak{a} the smallest vanishing order of ss along TT, where ss runs over all sections of 𝔞\mathfrak{a} at the generic point of TT. For a prime divisor TT over XX, i.e. a prime divisor on some birational model π:Y→X\pi:Y\to X, by μT​𝔞\mu_{T}\mathfrak{a} we mean μT​π∗​𝔞\mu_{T}\pi^{*}\mathfrak{a} and by μT​D\mu_{T}D we mean μT​π∗​D\mu_{T}\pi^{*}D in the case when DD is an ℝ\mathbb{R}-Cartier ℝ\mathbb{R}-divisor on XX.

2.2. Pairs and singularities

Definition 2.1

A sub-pair (X,B)(X,B) consists of a normal variety XX and an ℝ\mathbb{R}-divisor BB on XX such that KX+BK_{X}+B is ℝ\mathbb{R}-Cartier. A sub-pair (X,B)(X,B) is called a pair if BB is effective. If (X,B)(X,B) is a pair and the coefficients of BB are at most 11, we call BB a boundary on XX.

Definition 2.2

Let (X,B)(X,B) be a sub-pair and EE be a prime divisor on some birational model π:Y→X\pi:Y\to X. Denote by centerX⁡E\cent_{X}E the center of EE on XX, i.e. the image of EE on XX under the morphism π\pi. We may write KY+BY=π∗​(KX+B)K_{Y}+B_{Y}=\pi^{*}(K_{X}+B) for some uniquely determined BYB_{Y}. Then the log discrepancy a⁡(E,X,B)a(E,X,B) of EE with respect to (X,B)(X,B) is defined as 1−μE​BY1-\mu_{E}B_{Y}.

Definition 2.3

Let ϵ\epsilon be a non-negative real number. A sub-pair (X,B)(X,B) is said to be ϵ\epsilon-lc (resp. ϵ\epsilon-klt, lc, klt) if a⁡(E,X,B)≥ϵa(E,X,B)\geq\epsilon (resp. >ϵ>\epsilon, ≥0\geq 0, >0>0) for any prime divisor EE over XX. In the case when B=0B=0, we also say XX is ϵ\epsilon-lc (resp. ϵ\epsilon-klt, lc, klt). A pair (X,B)(X,B) is said to be plt (reps. ϵ\epsilon-plt) if a⁡(E,X,B)>0a(E,X,B)>0 (resp. >ϵ>\epsilon) for any exceptional prime divisor EE over XX.

Definition 2.4

A germ (X∋x,B)(X\ni x,B) consists of a pair (X,B)(X,B) and a closed point x∈Xx\in X. We say (X∋x,B)(X\ni x,B) is an ϵ\epsilon-lc (resp. ϵ\epsilon-klt, lc, klt) germ if (X,B)(X,B) is ϵ\epsilon-lc (resp. ϵ\epsilon-klt, lc, klt) near xx. When B=0B=0, we use X∋xX\ni x instead of (X∋x,0)(X\ni x,0).

Definition 2.5

Let (X,B)(X,B) be a sub-pair, f:X→Zf:X\to Z be a projective morphism and z∈Zz\in Z be a (not necessarily closed) point. We say (X,B)(X,B) is ϵ\epsilon-lc (or ϵ\epsilon-klt, lc, klt) over zz if (X,B)(X,B) is so over some neighbourhood of zz. We call EE a prime divisor over X/Z∋zX/Z\ni z if EE is a prime divisor over XX with f⁡(centerX⁡E)=z¯f(\cent_{X}E)=\overline{z} and we denote

mld(X/Z∋z,B):=inf{a(E,X,B)∣\displaystyle\mld(X/Z\ni z,B):=\inf\{a(E,X,B)\mid~ E is a prime divisor over X/Z∋z}.\displaystyle\text{$E$ is a prime divisor over $X/Z\ni z$}\}.

In the case when Z=XZ=X, z=xz=x and ff is the identity morphism, we call EE a prime divisor over X∋xX\ni x if EE is a prime divisor over XX with centerX⁡E=x¯\cent_{X}E=\overline{x} and we use mld⁡(X∋x,B)\mld(X\ni x,B) instead of mld(X/Z∋z,B)\mld(X/Z\ni z,B).

We remark that mld(X/Z∋z,B)≥0\mld(X/Z\ni z,B)\geq 0 if and only if (X,B)(X,B) is lc over zz (see [HJL22, Lemma 2.8]). However, mld(X/Z∋z,B)≥ϵ\mld(X/Z\ni z,B)\geq\epsilon is weaker than (X,B)(X,B) is ϵ\epsilon-lc over zz.

2.3. b-divisors

Let XX be a normal variety. A b-divisor D over XX is a collection of ℝ\mathbb{R}-divisors DY\textbf{D}_{Y} on YY, where YY runs over all birational models over XX, such that σ∗​DY1=DY2\sigma_{*}\textbf{D}_{Y_{1}}=\textbf{D}_{Y_{2}} for any birational morphism σ:Y1→Y2/X\sigma:Y_{1}\rightarrow Y_{2}/X.

Let 𝐃{\bf{D}} be a b-divisor over XX and Y0Y_{0} be a birational model over XX. We say 𝐃{\bf{D}} descends on Y0Y_{0} if DY0\textbf{D}_{Y_{0}} is an ℝ\mathbb{R}-Cartier ℝ\mathbb{R}-divisor and DY=σ∗​DY0\textbf{D}_{Y}=\sigma^{*}\textbf{D}_{Y_{0}} for any birational morphism σ:Y→Y0/X\sigma:Y\rightarrow Y_{0}/X.

Let X→UX\rightarrow U be a projective morphism. We say that a b-divisor D over XX is b-nef/U/U if 𝐃{\bf{D}} descends on some birational model Y0Y_{0} over XX and DY0\textbf{D}_{Y_{0}} is nef/U/U.

We denote by 0 the b-divisor 𝐃{\bf{D}} such that DY=0\textbf{D}_{Y}=0 for every birational model YY over XX.

2.4. Generalized pairs

Definition 2.6

A generalized sub-pair (g-sub-pair for short) (X,B+𝐌)/U(X,B+{\bf{M}})/U consists of a normal variety XX associated with a projective morphism X→UX\rightarrow U, an ℝ\mathbb{R}-divisor BB on XX, and a b-nef/U/U b-divisor 𝐌{\bf{M}} over XX. A g-sub-pair (X,B+𝐌)/U(X,B+{\bf{M}})/U is called a generalized pair (g-pair for short) if BB is effective.

We may drop UU when we emphasize the structures of (X,B+𝐌)(X,B+{\bf{M}}) that are independent of the choice of UU, for example, the singularities of (X,B+𝐌)(X,B+{\bf{M}}).

Definition 2.7

Let (X,B+𝐌)(X,B+{\bf{M}}) be a g-sub-pair and EE be a prime divisor on some birational model π:Y→X\pi:Y\to X. We can write

KY+BY+𝐌Y=π∗​(KX+B+𝐌X)K_{Y}+B_{Y}+{\bf{M}}_{Y}=\pi^{*}(K_{X}+B+{\bf{M}}_{X})

for some uniquely determined BYB_{Y}. Then the log discrepancy of EE with respect to (X,B+𝐌)(X,B+{\bf{M}}) is defined as 1−μE​BY1-\mu_{E}B_{Y} and denoted by a⁡(E,X,B+𝐌)a(E,X,B+{\bf{M}}).

Definition 2.8

Let ϵ\epsilon be a non-negative real number. A g-sub-pair (X,B+𝐌)(X,B+{\bf{M}}) is said to be ϵ\epsilon-lc (resp. ϵ\epsilon-klt, lc, klt) if a⁡(E,X,B+𝐌)≥ϵa(E,X,B+{\bf{M}})\geq\epsilon (resp. >ϵ>\epsilon, ≥0\geq 0, >0>0) for any prime divisor EE over XX.

In the case that 𝐌=0{\bf{M}}=\textbf{0}, all definitions of g-pairs coincide with those of usual pairs.

2.5. Canonical bundle formula

Let f:X→Zf:X\rightarrow Z be a contraction between normal varieties with dimZ>0\dim Z>0 and let Z→UZ\to U be a projective morphism. Let (X,B)(X,B) be a pair such that KX+B∼ℝ0/ZK_{X}+B\sim_{\mathbb{R}}0/Z and (X,B)(X,B) is lc over the generic point of ZZ. Then KX+B∼ℝf∗LK_{X}+B\sim_{\mathbb{R}}f^{*}L for some ℝ\mathbb{R}-Cartier ℝ\mathbb{R}-divisor LL on ZZ.

For any prime divisor DD on ZZ, denote by tDt_{D} the largest number such that (X,B+tD​f∗​D)(X,B+t_{D}f^{*}D) is lc over the generic point of DD. This makes sense even if DD is not ℚ\mathbb{Q}-Cartier because we only need the pullback of DD over the generic point of DD where ZZ is smooth. We set BZ=∑D(1−tD)​DB_{Z}=\sum_{D}(1-t_{D})D where DD runs over all prime divisors on ZZ and set MZ=L−KZ−BZM_{Z}=L-K_{Z}-B_{Z}. The former is called the discriminant divisor and the latter is called the moduli divisor. By construction, we have the so called canonical bundle formula

KX+B∼ℝf∗(KZ+BZ+MZ).K_{X}+B\sim_{\mathbb{R}}f^{*}(K_{Z}+B_{Z}+M_{Z}).

Let σ:Z′→Z\sigma:Z^{\prime}\rightarrow Z be a birational morphism from a normal variety Z′Z^{\prime} and let X′X^{\prime} be a resolution of the main component of X×ZZ′X\times_{Z}Z^{\prime} with induced morphisms τ:X′→X\tau:X^{\prime}\rightarrow X and f′:X′→Z′f^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\rightarrow Z^{\prime}. Write KX′+B′=τ∗​(KX+B)K_{X^{\prime}}+B^{\prime}=\tau^{*}(K_{X}+B), then KX′+B′∼ℝf′⁣∗σ∗LK_{X^{\prime}}+B^{\prime}\sim_{\mathbb{R}}f^{\prime*}\sigma^{*}L. Similarly we can define the discriminant divisor BZ′B_{Z^{\prime}} and the moduli divisor MZ′M_{Z^{\prime}} for the contraction (X′,B′)→Z′(X^{\prime},B^{\prime})\rightarrow Z^{\prime}. One can check that σ∗​BZ′=BZ\sigma_{*}B_{Z^{\prime}}=B_{Z} and σ∗​MZ′=MZ\sigma_{*}M_{Z^{\prime}}=M_{Z}. Hence there exist b-divisors 𝐁,𝐌{\bf{B}},{\bf{M}} over ZZ such that 𝐁Z′=BZ′{\bf{B}}_{Z^{\prime}}=B_{Z^{\prime}} and 𝐌Z′=MZ′{\bf{M}}_{Z^{\prime}}=M_{Z^{\prime}} for any birational model Z′Z^{\prime} over ZZ, which are called the discriminant b-divisor and the moduli b-divisor respectively.

It was shown by Kawamata [Ka97, Ka98] and Ambro [Am04, Am05] that 𝐌{\bf{M}} is a b-nef/U/U b-divisor over ZZ (see [Hu21, Section 3] for ℝ\mathbb{R}-coefficients). Thus we can regard (Z,BZ+𝐌)/U(Z,B_{Z}+{\bf{M}})/U as a g-pair. We call (Z,BZ+𝐌)/U(Z,B_{Z}+{\bf{M}})/U the g-pair induced by the canonical bundle formula for (X,B)→Z/U(X,B)\rightarrow Z/U.

Lemma 2.9.

Keep the notation and assumptions as above. If (Z,BZ+𝐌)(Z,B_{Z}+{\bf{M}}) is an lc g-pair, then (X,B)(X,B) is lc.

Proof.

Suppose that (X,B)(X,B) is not lc. Since (X,B)(X,B) is lc over the generic point of ZZ by assumption, there is a prime divisor SS over XX such that a⁡(S,X,B)<0a(S,X,B)<0 and SS is vertical over ZZ. By [Bi19, Lemma 3.7], there is a prime divisor TT over ZZ such that a⁡(T,Z,BZ+𝐌)<0a(T,Z,B_{Z}+{\bf{M}})<0. This contradicts the hypothesis that (Z,BZ+𝐌)(Z,B_{Z}+{\bf{M}}) is an lc g-pair. ∎

Lemma 2.10.

Keep the notation and assumptions as above. Let tt be a non-negative number and HH be an effective ℝ\mathbb{R}-Cartier divisor on ZZ. If (Z,BZ+t​H+𝐌)(Z,B_{Z}+tH+{\bf{M}}) is an lc g-pair, then (X,B+t​f∗​H)(X,B+tf^{*}H) is lc.

Proof.

By [PS09, Lemma 7.4(iii)], (Z,BZ+t​H+𝐌)(Z,B_{Z}+tH+{\bf{M}}) is the g-pair induced by the canonical bundle formula for (X,B+t​f∗​H)→Z(X,B+tf^{*}H)\rightarrow Z. Thus the lemma follows from Lemma 2.9. ∎

2.6. Fano type fibrations

Let X→ZX\to Z be a contraction between normal varieties. We say XX is of Fano type over ZZ if one of the following three equivalent conditions holds ([PS09, Lemma-Definition 2.6]):

  • •

    there is a klt pair (X,C)(X,C) such that −(KX+C)-(K_{X}+C) is ample over ZZ,

  • •

    there is a klt pair (X,C)(X,C) such that −(KX+C)-(K_{X}+C) is big and nef over ZZ, and

  • •

    −KX-K_{X} is big over ZZ and there is a klt pair (X,C)(X,C) such that KX+C∼ℝ0/ZK_{X}+C\sim_{\mathbb{R}}0/Z.

Assume XX is of Fano type over ZZ and DD is an ℝ\mathbb{R}-Cartier ℝ\mathbb{R}-divisor on XX. By the base point free theorem, if DD is nef over ZZ, then DD is semi-ample over ZZ. In particular, if D≡0/ZD\equiv 0/Z, then D∼ℝ0/ZD\sim_{\mathbb{R}}0/Z. By [BCHM], one can run an MMP on DD over ZZ and the MMP ends with a good minimal model or a Mori fiber space over ZZ.

Lemma 2.11.

[PS09, Lemma 2.8] Suppose that XX is of Fano type over ZZ.

(1) Suppose X⇢X′/ZX\dashrightarrow X^{\prime}/Z is a birational map whose inverse does not contract any divisor. Then X′X^{\prime} is of Fano type over ZZ.

(2) Suppose X→Y/ZX\to Y/Z is a contraction of varieties over ZZ. Then YY is of Fano type over ZZ.

(3) Let (X,B)(X,B) be an lc pair such that −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ. Let YY be a normal variety with a projective birational morphism Y→XY\to X and let KY+BYK_{Y}+B_{Y} be the pullback of KX+BK_{X}+B. If every exceptional/X/X component of BYB_{Y} has positive coefficient, then YY is of Fano type over ZZ.

2.7. Complements

Definition 2.12

Let X→ZX\to Z be a contraction and (X,B)(X,B) be a pair. A monotonic lc (resp. klt) nn-complement of KX+BK_{X}+B over a point z∈Zz\in Z is of the form KX+ΛK_{X}+\Lambda such that over some neighbourhood of zz we have

  • •

    Λ≥B\Lambda\geq B,

  • •

    (X,Λ)(X,\Lambda) is lc (resp. klt), and

  • •

    n⁡(KX+Λ)∼0/Zn(K_{X}+\Lambda)\sim 0/Z.

2.8. Triples

Definition 2.13

A triple (X,B,𝔞t)(X,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t}) consists of a pair (X,B)(X,B) and a non-zero ideal sheaf 𝔞\mathfrak{a} on XX with a non-negative exponent tt.

Definition 2.14

Let (X,B,𝔞t)(X,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t}) be a triple and EE be a prime divisor on some birational model π:Y→X\pi:Y\to X. We may write KY+BY=π∗​(KX+B)K_{Y}+B_{Y}=\pi^{*}(K_{X}+B) for some uniquely determined BYB_{Y}. The log discrepancy a⁡(E,X,B,𝔞t)a(E,X,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t}) of EE with respect to (X,B,𝔞t)(X,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t}) is defined by

a⁡(E,X,B,𝔞t):=1−μE​BY−t⋅μE​π∗​𝔞.a(E,X,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t}):=1-\mu_{E}B_{Y}-t\cdot\mu_{E}\pi^{*}\mathfrak{a}.
Definition 2.15

Let ϵ\epsilon be a non-negative real number. A triple (X,B,𝔞t)(X,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t}) is said to be ϵ\epsilon-lc (resp. ϵ\epsilon-klt, lc, klt) if a⁡(E,X,B,𝔞t)≥ϵa(E,X,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t})\geq\epsilon (resp. >ϵ>\epsilon, ≥0\geq 0, >0>0) for any prime divisor EE over XX.

Definition 2.16

Let (X,B,𝔞t)(X,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t}) be a triple, f:X→Zf:X\rightarrow Z be a projective morphism and z∈Zz\in Z be a (not necessary closed) point. We say (X,B,𝔞t)(X,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t}) is ϵ\epsilon-lc (or ϵ\epsilon-klt, lc, klt) over zz if (X,B,𝔞t)(X,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t}) is so over some neighbourhood of zz. We denote

mld(X/Z∋z,B,𝔞t):=inf{a(E,X,B,𝔞t)∣\displaystyle\mld(X/Z\ni z,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t}):=\inf\{a(E,X,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t})\mid~ E is a prime divisor over X/Z∋z}.\displaystyle\text{$E$ is a prime divisor over $X/Z\ni z$}\}.

(Recall that a prime divisor EE over X/Z∋zX/Z\ni z means a prime divisor EE over XX with f⁡(centerX⁡E)=z¯f(\cent_{X}E)=\overline{z}, see Definition 2.5.) In the case that Z=XZ=X, z=xz=x and ff is the identity morphism, we will use mld⁡(X∋x,B,𝔞t)\mld(X\ni x,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t}) instead of mld(X/Z∋z,B,𝔞t)\mld(X/Z\ni z,B,\mathfrak{a}^{t}).

In the case that 𝔞=𝒪X\mathfrak{a}=\mathcal{O}_{X}, all definitions of triples coincide with those of usual pairs.

Lemma 2.17.

Let f:X→Zf:X\to Z be a contraction with dimZ>0\dim Z>0, (X,B)(X,B) be a pair, z∈Zz\in Z be a closed point and tt be a non-negative number. Denote by 𝔪z\mathfrak{m}_{z} the ideal sheaf of the closed point z∈Zz\in Z. Let VzV_{z} be a linear system on ZZ such that

  • •

    all the elements of VzV_{z} contain zz,

  • •

    the local defining equations of elements of VzV_{z} generate 𝔪z\mathfrak{m}_{z} near zz, and

    VzV_{z} is base point free outside zz.

Then the following holds.

  1. (1)

    Let TT be a prime divisor over X/Z∋zX/Z\ni z. Then

    a⁡(T,X,B,f∗​𝔪zt)=a⁡(T,X,B+t​f∗​H)a(T,X,B,f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t})=a(T,X,B+tf^{*}H)

    for a general element H∈VzH\in V_{z}.

  2. (2)

    If t≤1t\leq 1, then

    mld(X/Z∋z,B,f∗𝔪zt)=mld(X/Z∋z,B+tf∗H)\mld(X/Z\ni z,B,f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t})=\mld(X/Z\ni z,B+tf^{*}H)

    for a general element H∈VzH\in V_{z}.

  3. (3)

    Let ϵ\epsilon be a real number in [0,1][0,1]. If (X,B,f∗​𝔪zt)(X,B,f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t}) is ϵ\epsilon-lc and t≤1−ϵt\leq 1-\epsilon, then (X,B+t​f∗​H)(X,B+tf^{*}H) is ϵ\epsilon-lc for a general element H∈VzH\in V_{z}.

Remark 2.18

A linear system satisfying the conditions in Lemma 2.17 always exists. Indeed, since ZZ is assumed to be quasi-projective, we can find a compactification Z¯\bar{Z} of ZZ which is projective. Let AA be a very ample divisor on Z¯\bar{Z} and let VzV_{z} be the sub-linear system of A|ZA|_{Z} consisting of elements containing zz. Then VzV_{z} satisfies the conditions.

Proof.

(1) As the defining equations of elements in VzV_{z} generate 𝔪z\mathfrak{m}_{z} near zz, there is H∈VzH\in V_{z} such that μT​f∗​H=μT​f∗​𝔪z\mu_{T}f^{*}H=\mu_{T}f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z} and thus the first assertion follows.

(2) Let π:W→X\pi:W\to X be a resolution of XX such that π∗​f∗​𝔪z\pi^{*}f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z} is a locally principle ideal sheaf on WW, that is, there exists an effective divisor FF on WW such that

π∗​f∗​𝔪z=𝒪W​(−F).\pi^{*}f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}=\mathcal{O}_{W}(-F).

For any element H∈VzH\in V_{z}, we have π∗​f∗​H≥F\pi^{*}f^{*}H\geq F. Write KW+BW=π∗​(KX+B)K_{W}+B_{W}=\pi^{*}(K_{X}+B). Then

mld(W/Z∋z,BW+tF)=mld(X/Z∋z,B,𝔪zt).\mld(W/Z\ni z,B_{W}+tF)=\mld(X/Z\ni z,B,\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t}).

Let LzL_{z} be the linear system on WW defined by

Lz:={π∗​f∗​H−F∣H∈Vz}.L_{z}:=\{\pi^{*}f^{*}H-F\mid H\in V_{z}\}.

We claim that LzL_{z} is base point free. Indeed, for any closed point p∈π−1​f−1​z=Supp⁡Fp\in\pi^{-1}f^{-1}z=\Supp F, there is an element P∈VzP\in V_{z} such that the local defining equation of π∗​f∗​P\pi^{*}f^{*}P generates 𝒪W​(−F)\mathcal{O}_{W}(-F) in a neighbourhood of pp, because the local defining equations of elements in VzV_{z} generate 𝔪z\mathfrak{m}_{z} near zz and because π∗​f∗​𝔪z=𝒪W​(−F)\pi^{*}f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}=\mathcal{O}_{W}(-F). Thus π∗​f∗​P=F\pi^{*}f^{*}P=F near pp, which implies that π∗​f∗​P−F\pi^{*}f^{*}P-F does not contain pp. So LzL_{z} is base point free on a neighbourhood of pp for any closed point p∈π−1​f−1​zp\in\pi^{-1}f^{-1}z, which implies that LzL_{z} is base point free over a neighbourhood of zz. As VzV_{z} is base point free outside zz, LzL_{z} is base point free everywhere.

Let HH be a general element of VzV_{z}. Then R:=π∗​f∗​H−FR:=\pi^{*}f^{*}H-F is a general element of LzL_{z}. We have

mld(X/Z∋z,B+tf∗H)=mld(W/Z∋z,BW+tπ∗f∗H)\displaystyle\mld(X/Z\ni z,B+tf^{*}H)=\mld(W/Z\ni z,B_{W}+t\pi^{*}f^{*}H)
=\displaystyle= mld(W/Z∋z,BW+tF+tR)=mld(W/Z∋z,BW+tF)\displaystyle\mld(W/Z\ni z,B_{W}+tF+tR)=\mld(W/Z\ni z,B_{W}+tF)
=\displaystyle= mld(X/Z∋z,B,𝔪zt).\displaystyle\mld(X/Z\ni z,B,\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t}).

The second equality in the second low holds because t≤1t\leq 1 and LzL_{z} is base point free.

(3) Let HH be a general element of VzV_{z}. Since (X,B,f∗​𝔪zt)(X,B,f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t}) is ϵ\epsilon-lc, (X,B)(X,B) is ϵ\epsilon-lc. It follows that (X,B+t​f∗​H)(X,B+tf^{*}H) is ϵ\epsilon-lc outside f−1​zf^{-1}z as VzV_{z} is base point free outside zz and as t≤1−ϵt\leq 1-\epsilon. By (2) we have

mld(X/Z∋z,B+tf∗H)=mld(X/Z∋z,B,f∗𝔪zt)≥ϵ.\mld(X/Z\ni z,B+tf^{*}H)=\mld(X/Z\ni z,B,f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t})\geq\epsilon.

Therefore, for any prime divisor TT over XX, no matter its image on ZZ is zz or not, we have a⁡(T,X,B+t​f∗​H)≥ϵa(T,X,B+tf^{*}H)\geq\epsilon. So (X,B+t​f∗​H)(X,B+tf^{*}H) is ϵ\epsilon-lc. ∎

Corollary 2.19.

Let f:X→Zf:X\to Z be a contraction with dimZ>0\dim Z>0, (X,B)(X,B) be a pair, z∈Zz\in Z be a closed point and tt be a non-negative number. Denote by 𝔪z\mathfrak{m}_{z} the ideal sheaf of z∈Zz\in Z. The following are equivalent.

  1. (1)

    There is an effective Cartier divisor HH on some neighbourhood of z∈Zz\in Z such that z∈Supp⁡Hz\in\Supp H and (X,B+t​f∗​H)(X,B+tf^{*}H) is lc over zz.

  2. (2)

    There is an effective Cartier divisor HH on ZZ such that z∈Supp⁡Hz\in\Supp H and (X,B+t​f∗​H)(X,B+tf^{*}H) is lc over zz.

  3. (3)

    (X,B,f∗​𝔪zt)(X,B,f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t}) is lc over zz.

Proof.

It is obvious that (2) implies (1) and (1) implies (3). So it suffices to show that (3) implies (2). Assume that (X,B,𝔪zt)(X,B,\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t}) is lc over zz. By Lemma 2.17(2) and Remark 2.18, there is an effective Cartier divisor HH on ZZ such that z∈Supp⁡Hz\in\Supp H and

mld(X/Z∋z,B+tf∗H)=mld(X/Z∋z,B,𝔪zt)≥0.\mld(X/Z\ni z,B+tf^{*}H)=\mld(X/Z\ni z,B,\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t})\geq 0.

Thus (X,B+t​f∗​H)(X,B+tf^{*}H) is lc over zz. ∎

2.9. Rational surface singularities

Definition 2.20

Let ZZ be a normal variety with a closed point zz. We say Z∋zZ\ni z is a rational singularity if for any resolution π:Y→Z\pi:Y\to Z the following holds near zz:

Ri​π∗​𝒪Y=0,for any ​i>0.R^{i}\pi_{*}\mathcal{O}_{Y}=0,\quad\text{for any }i>0.

Moreover, if dimZ=2\dim Z=2, we say Z∋zZ\ni z is a rational surface singularity.

Lemma 2.21.

[Br68, Lemma 1.3] Let Z∋zZ\ni z be a rational surface singularity and let Y→ZY\to Z be a resolution. Denote by EE the exceptional divisor on YY over Z∋zZ\ni z. Then EE is a simple normal crossing divisor and each component of EE is a smooth rational curve.

Definition-Lemma 2.22.

[Ar66, pp. 131-132] Let ZZ be a normal surface with a closed point zz. Let π:Y→Z\pi:Y\to Z be a resolution with the exceptional divisor E=∪i=1rEiE=\cup_{i=1}^{r}E_{i} over Z∋zZ\ni z. Denote by 𝒮\mathcal{S} the set

{C=∑i=1raiEi∣ai∈ℤ≥0,C≠0,C⋅Ek≤0 for k=1,⋯r}.\{C=\sum_{i=1}^{r}a_{i}E_{i}\mid a_{i}\in\mathbb{Z}^{\geq 0},~C\neq 0,~C\cdot E_{k}\leq 0\text{ for }k=1,\cdots r\}.

Then 𝒮\mathcal{S} has a minimum element, that is, an element Cf∈𝒮C_{f}\in\mathcal{S} such that C≥CfC\geq C_{f} for any C∈𝒮C\in\mathcal{S}. We call this minimum element the fundamental cycle of Z∋zZ\ni z on YY.

Remark 2.23

It is obvious that the fundamental cycle is determined by the intersection matrix (Ei⋅Ej)i,j=1r(E_{i}\cdot E_{j})^{r}_{i,j=1}.

Remark 2.24

Laufer [La72, Proposition 4.1] developed an algorithm to compute the fundamental cycle CfC_{f} as follows.

(1) Begin with any of the components of the exceptional divisor C1:=Ei0.C_{1}:=E_{i_{0}}.
Assume that ClC_{l} is already defined for some l>0l>0. There are two cases.

(2) If Cl⋅Ek≤0C_{l}\cdot E_{k}\leq 0 for any kk, then we stop and ClC_{l} is the fundamental cycle.

(3) If there is a component EilE_{i_{l}} such that Cl⋅Eil>0C_{l}\cdot E_{i_{l}}>0, then set Cl+1:=Cl+EilC_{l+1}:=C_{l}+E_{i_{l}} and repeat the above process.

Lemma 2.25.

[Ar66, Theorem 4] Let Z∋zZ\ni z be a rational surface singularity. Let π:Y→Z\pi:Y\to Z be a resolution and denote by 𝔪z\mathfrak{m}_{z} the ideal sheaf of the closed point z∈Zz\in Z. Then

π∗​𝔪z=𝒪Y​(−Cf),\pi^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}=\mathcal{O}_{Y}(-C_{f}),

where CfC_{f} is the fundamental cycle of Z∋zZ\ni z on YY.

2.10. Toric varieties

A toric variety is a normal variety XX of dimension dd that contains a torus TXT_{X} (that is, isomorphic to (ℂ∗)d(\mathbb{C}^{*})^{d}) as a dense open subset, together with an action TX×X→XT_{X}\times X\to X of TXT_{X} on XX that extends the natural action of TXT_{X} on itself.

A toric morphism is a morphism f:X→Yf:X\to Y between toric varieties such that ff maps the torus TX⊂XT_{X}\subset X into TY⊂YT_{Y}\subset Y and f|TXf|_{T_{X}} is a group homomorphism.

A toric contraction is a contraction f:X→Yf:X\to Y so that ff is a toric morphism. We remark that if f:X→Yf:X\to Y is a toric contraction, then XX is of Fano type over YY.

A toric pair is a pair (X,B)(X,B) so that XX is a toric variety and BB is invariant under the torus action of TXT_{X}.

We refer to [Fu93] or [CLS11] for the general theory of toric varieties.

2.11. Exceptional singularities

Definition 2.26

Let (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) be a klt germ. A plt (resp. δ\delta-plt) blow-up of (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) is a birational morphism π:Y→Z\pi:Y\to Z such that

  • •

    YY has a prime divisor EE such that centerZ⁡E=z\cent_{Z}E=z and −E-E is ample over ZZ (in particular, Ex​(π)=E\text{Ex}(\pi)=E, where Ex​(π)\text{Ex}(\pi) is the exceptional locus of π\pi);

  • •

    (Y,E+ΔY)(Y,E+\Delta_{Y}) is plt (resp. δ\delta-plt) near EE, where ΔY\Delta_{Y} is the birational transform of Δ\Delta on YY.

Lemma 2.27.

[HLS19, Lemma 3.12] Any klt germ (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) with dimZ≥2\dim Z\geq 2 has a plt blow-up.

Definition 2.28

Let (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) be an lc germ. We say (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) is an exceptional singularity, if for any effective ℝ\mathbb{R}-divisor GG on ZZ so that (Z∋z,Δ+G)(Z\ni z,\Delta+G) is lc, there exists at most one prime divisor EE over ZZ such that a⁡(E,Z,Δ+G)=0a(E,Z,\Delta+G)=0 and z∈centerZ⁡Ez\in\cent_{Z}E. Moreover, if (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) is a klt germ, we say (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) is a klt exceptional singularity. In the case when Δ=0\Delta=0, we use Z∋zZ\ni z instead of (Z∋z,0)(Z\ni z,0).

Lemma 2.29.

[HLS19, Lemma 3.16] Let (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) be a klt exceptional singularity with dimZ≥2\dim Z\geq 2. Then (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) has a unique plt blow-up.

Lemma 2.30.

[HLS19, Lemma 3.22] Let s≥2s\geq 2 be an integer and 𝔇⊂[0,1]\mathfrak{D}\subset[0,1] be a DCC set. Then there exists a positive real number δ\delta depending only on ss and 𝔇\mathfrak{D} satisfying the following. Let (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) be a klt exceptional singularity so that dimZ=s\dim Z=s and the coefficients of Δ\Delta are in 𝔇\mathfrak{D}. Let f:Y→Zf:Y\to Z be the unique plt blow-up of (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta). Then f:Y→Zf:Y\to Z is a δ\delta-plt blow-up of (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta).

3. Proof of (5) ⇒\Rightarrow (3) in Theorem 1.6

The goal of this section is to show that Conjecture 1.4 implies Conjecture 1.3. Theorem 1.1 in [Bi23] plays a key role in the proof. We begin with a generalized version of Conjecture 1.4.

Conjecture 3.1.

Let ss be a natural number and ϵ\epsilon be a positive real number. Then there is a positive number tt depending only on s,ϵs,\epsilon satisfying the following. Assume (Z,Δ+𝐍)(Z,\Delta+{\bf{N}}) is an ϵ\epsilon-lc g-pair of dimension ss with a closed point z∈Zz\in Z. Then there exists an effective Cartier divisor HH on some neighbourhood of z∈Zz\in Z such that z∈Supp⁡Hz\in\Supp H and (Z,Δ+t​H+𝐍)(Z,\Delta+tH+{\bf{N}}) is lc near zz.

Proposition 3.2.

Assume Conjecture 1.4 holds in dimension ≤ℓ\leq\ell for some natural number ℓ\ell. Then Conjecture 3.1 holds in dimension ≤ℓ\leq\ell.

Proof.

Let (Z,Δ+𝐍)(Z,\Delta+{\bf{N}}) be an ϵ\epsilon-lc g-pair of dimension s≤ℓs\leq\ell. Take a high enough birational model π:Z′→Z\pi:Z^{\prime}\to Z such that 𝐍{\bf{N}} descends on Z′Z^{\prime} and 𝐍Z′{\bf{N}}_{Z^{\prime}} is nef over ZZ. Write

KZ′+Δ′+𝐍Z′=π∗​(KZ+Δ+𝐍Z).K_{Z^{\prime}}+\Delta^{\prime}+{\bf{N}}_{Z^{\prime}}=\pi^{*}(K_{Z}+\Delta+{\bf{N}}_{Z}).

Then (Z′,Δ′)(Z^{\prime},\Delta^{\prime}) is an ϵ\epsilon-lc sub-pair. where E=π∗​E′E=\pi_{*}E^{\prime}. So (Z,Δ+E)(Z,\Delta+E) is an ϵ2\frac{\epsilon}{2}-lc pair. By the assumption that Conjecture 1.4 holds, for any closed point z∈Zz\in Z, there exists an effective Cartier divisor HH on some neighbourhood of z∈Zz\in Z such that z∈Supp⁡Hz\in\Supp H and (Z,Δ+E+t​H)(Z,\Delta+E+tH) is lc near zz, where t>0t>0 only depends on s,ϵs,\epsilon. For any prime divisor DD over ZZ with z∈centerZ⁡Dz\in\cent_{Z}D, we have

a⁡(D,Z,Δ+t​H+𝐍)\displaystyle a(D,Z,\Delta+tH+{\bf{N}}) =a⁡(D,Z′,Δ′+t​π∗​H)≥a⁡(D,Z′,Δ′+E′+t​π∗​H)\displaystyle=a(D,Z^{\prime},\Delta^{\prime}+t\pi^{*}H)\geq a(D,Z^{\prime},\Delta^{\prime}+E^{\prime}+t\pi^{*}H)
=a⁡(D,Z,Δ+E+t​H)≥0.\displaystyle=a(D,Z,\Delta+E+tH)\geq 0.

Hence the g-pair (Z,Δ+t​H+𝐍)(Z,\Delta+tH+{\bf{N}}) is lc near zz. ∎

Proposition 3.3.

Assume Conjecture 1.4 holds in dimension ≤ℓ\leq\ell for some natural number ℓ\ell. Then Conjecture 1.3 holds when dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell.

Proof.

Let (X,B)(X,B) be a pair, f:X→Zf:X\to Z be a contraction with dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell and z∈Zz\in Z be a closed point satisfying the conditions in Conjecture 1.3. By [Bi23, Theorem 1.1], (Z,Δ+𝐍)(Z,\Delta+{\bf{N}}) is δ\delta-lc, where δ>0\delta>0 only depends on d,ϵd,\epsilon. Thus tt only depends on d,ϵd,\epsilon as dimZ≤dimX=d\dim Z\leq\dim X=d and as δ\delta only depends on d,ϵd,\epsilon. By Lemma 2.10, (X,B+E+t​f∗​H)(X,B+E+tf^{*}H) is lc, which implies that (X,B+t​f∗​H)(X,B+tf^{*}H) is lc. ∎

4. Proof of (3) ⇒\Rightarrow (1) in Theorem 1.6

The goal of this section is to prove that Conjecture 1.3 implies Conjecture 1.1. Many techniques used in this section come from [Bi22]. We begin with a definition introduced by Birkar in [Bi22].

Definition 4.1

Let d,rd,r be natural numbers and ϵ\epsilon be a positive real number. A (d,r,ϵ)(d,r,\epsilon)-Fano type fibration consists of a pair (X,Γ)(X,\Gamma) and a contraction f:X→Zf:X\to Z such that

  • •

    (X,Γ)(X,\Gamma) is a projective ϵ\epsilon-lc pair of dimension dd,

  • •

    KX+Γ∼ℝf∗LK_{X}+\Gamma\sim_{\mathbb{R}}f^{*}L for some ℝ\mathbb{R}-Cartier ℝ\mathbb{R}-divisor LL on ZZ,

  • •

    −KX-K_{X} is big over ZZ, i.e. XX is of Fano type over ZZ,

  • •

    AA is a very ample divisor on ZZ with AdimZ≤rA^{\dim Z}\leq r, and

  • •

    A−LA-L is ample.

The following proposition is the same as [Bi21, Theorem 1.9] except that we remove the condition that M−(KX+B)M-(K_{X}+B) is big. We follow the argument in the proof of [Bi21, Theorem 1.9] with small modifications.

Proposition 4.2.

Let d,pd,p be natural numbers. Then there exists a natural number nn depending only on d,pd,p satisfying the following. Assume

  • •

    (X,B)(X,B) is a projective lc pair of dimension dd,

  • •

    p​BpB is integral,

  • •

    f:X→Zf:X\to Z is a contraction,

  • •

    MM is the pullback of an ample Cartier divisor on ZZ,

  • •

    XX is of Fano type over ZZ,

  • •

    M−(KX+B)M-(K_{X}+B) is nef, and

  • •

    SS is a non-klt center of (X,B)(X,B) whose image on ZZ is a closed point.

Then there is a ℚ\mathbb{Q}-divisor Λ≥B\Lambda\geq B such that

  • •

    (X,Λ)(X,\Lambda) is lc over a neighbourhood of z:=f⁡(S)z:=f(S), and

  • •

    n⁡(KX+Λ)∼(n+2)​Mn(K_{X}+\Lambda)\sim(n+2)M.

Proof.

By the proof of [Bi21, Proposition 4.1], Proposition 4.2 holds under an additional assumption that there is a boundary Γ\Gamma on XX such that

  • •

    (X,Γ)(X,\Gamma) is plt with S=⌊Γ⌋S=\lfloor\Gamma\rfloor, and

  • •

    −(KX+Γ)-(K_{X}+\Gamma) is ample over ZZ.

Note that the condition that M−(KX+B)M-(K_{X}+B) is big has not been used in the proof of [Bi21, Proposition 4.1]. So it suffices to construct a boundary Γ\Gamma satisfying the above conditions.

Replacing (X,B)(X,B) with a ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorial dlt model, we may assume that XX is ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorial and SS is a component of ⌊B⌋\lfloor B\rfloor. The Fano type property of XX over ZZ is preserved by Lemma 2.11 since −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ. As −KX-K_{X} is big over ZZ and as SS is vertical over ZZ, −(KX+S)-(K_{X}+S) is big over ZZ.

As −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ and as XX is of Fano type over ZZ, −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is semi-ample over ZZ. Let X→U/ZX\to U/Z be the contraction defining by −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) over ZZ. Then KX+B∼ℚ0/UK_{X}+B\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}0/U. As −(KX+S)-(K_{X}+S) is big over ZZ, it is also big over UU. Run an MMP on −(KX+S)-(K_{X}+S) over UU and let X′X^{\prime} be the resulting model. In this process SS is not contracted because

B−S∼ℚ−(KX+S)/UB-S\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}-(K_{X}+S)/U

and because SS is not a component of B−SB-S. Let X′→X′′/UX^{\prime}\to X^{\prime\prime}/U be the contraction defined by −(KX′+S′)-(K_{X^{\prime}}+S^{\prime}) over UU, where S′S^{\prime} is the pushdown of SS to X′X^{\prime}. Then X′→X′′X^{\prime}\to X^{\prime\prime} is birational as −(KX+S)-(K_{X}+S) is big over UU. We claim that S′S^{\prime} is not contracted over X′′X^{\prime\prime}. Indeed, if not, since KX′+S′∼ℚ0/X′′K_{X^{\prime}}+S^{\prime}\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}0/X^{\prime\prime}, the pair (X′′,0)(X^{\prime\prime},0) would not be klt. As X′′X^{\prime\prime} is of Fano type over ZZ by Lemma 2.11, there is a klt pair on X′′X^{\prime\prime}, which leads to a contradiction.

Assume that there exist n∈ℕn\in\mathbb{N} and Λ′′≥B′′\Lambda^{\prime\prime}\geq B^{\prime\prime} such that (X′′,Λ′′)(X^{\prime\prime},\Lambda^{\prime\prime}) is lc over zz and

n⁡(KX′′+Λ′′)∼(n+2)​M′′,n(K_{X^{\prime\prime}}+\Lambda^{\prime\prime})\sim(n+2)M^{\prime\prime},

where B′′,M′′B^{\prime\prime},M^{\prime\prime} are the pushdowns of B,MB,M to X′′X^{\prime\prime}. Since KX+B∼ℚ0/UK_{X}+B\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}0/U, taking the crepant pullback of KX′′+Λ′′K_{X^{\prime\prime}}+\Lambda^{\prime\prime} to XX, we get Λ≥B\Lambda\geq B such that (X,Λ)(X,\Lambda) is lc over zz and

n⁡(KX+Λ)∼(n+2)​M.n(K_{X}+\Lambda)\sim(n+2)M.

Thus we can replace XX with X′′X^{\prime\prime} and assume that −(KX+S)-(K_{X}+S) is ample over UU. The ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorial property of XX may be lost but we will not use it any more. Every non-klt center of (X,S)(X,S) is contained in SS because XX admits a klt pair as XX is of Fano type over ZZ.

Let Δ=(1−b)​B+b​S\Delta=(1-b)B+bS for a sufficiently small real number b>0b>0. Then any non-klt place of (X,Δ)(X,\Delta) is also a non-klt place of (X,S)(X,S), and hence its center on XX is contained in SS and is mapped to zz. Since −(KX+S)-(K_{X}+S) is ample over UU and −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is ℚ\mathbb{Q}-linear equivalent to the pullback of an ample/Z/Z ℚ\mathbb{Q}-divisor on UU, we have

−(KX+Δ)=−(1−b)​(KX+B)−b⁡(KX+S)-(K_{X}+\Delta)=-(1-b)(K_{X}+B)-b(K_{X}+S)

is ample over ZZ.

By [Bi21, Lemma 2.7] applied to (X,Δ)(X,\Delta), there is a prime divisor TT over XX and a birational morphism Y→XY\to X such that

  • •

    either Y→XY\to X is small or it contracts TT but no other divisors,

  • •

    (Y,T)(Y,T) is plt,

  • •

    −(KY+T)-(K_{Y}+T) is ample over XX, and

  • •

    a⁡(T,X,Δ)=0a(T,X,\Delta)=0.

In particular, TT is mapped to zz since it is a non-klt place of (X,Δ)(X,\Delta). Since Δ≤B\Delta\leq B, we have a⁡(T,X,B)=0a(T,X,B)=0.

Let KY+ΔYK_{Y}+\Delta_{Y} be the pullback of KX+ΔK_{X}+\Delta to YY and let

Γ=(1−c)​ΔY+c​T\Gamma=(1-c)\Delta_{Y}+cT

for some sufficiently small c>0c>0. Since −(KX+Δ)-(K_{X}+\Delta) is ample over ZZ and −(KY+T)-(K_{Y}+T) is ample over XX, we have

−(KY+Γ)=−(1−c)​(KY+ΔY)−c⁡(KY+T)-(K_{Y}+\Gamma)=-(1-c)(K_{Y}+\Delta_{Y})-c(K_{Y}+T)

is ample over ZZ. Moreover, (Y,Γ)(Y,\Gamma) is plt and T=⌊Γ⌋T=\lfloor\Gamma\rfloor is mapped to zz.

Let KY+BYK_{Y}+B_{Y}, MYM_{Y} be the pullbacks of KX+BK_{X}+B, MM to YY. Replace (X,B),M,S(X,B),M,S with (Y,BY),MY,T(Y,B_{Y}),M_{Y},T. Then there is a boundary Γ\Gamma on XX such that (X,Γ)(X,\Gamma) is plt with S=⌊Γ⌋S=\lfloor\Gamma\rfloor and −(KX+Γ)-(K_{X}+\Gamma) is ample over ZZ. ∎

The following proposition is the same as [Bi22, Proposition 4.15] except that we remove the condition that −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is big over ZZ and we emphasize that nn is independent of r,ϵr,\epsilon. The notation is also slightly different; B,ΓB,\Gamma in the following proposition correspond to Δ,B\Delta,B in [Bi22, Proposition 4.15] respectively. We follow the argument in the proof of [Bi22, Proposition 4.15] with small modifications.

Proposition 4.3.

Let d,rd,r be natural numbers, ϵ\epsilon be a positive real number and ℜ⊂[0,1]\mathfrak{R}\subset[0,1] be a finite set of rational numbers. Then there exist a natural number nn depending on d,ℜd,\mathfrak{R} and a natural number mm depending on d,r,ϵ,ℜd,r,\epsilon,\mathfrak{R} satisfying the following (note that nn is independent of r,ϵr,\epsilon). Let VzV_{z} be the sub-linear system of |f∗​A||f^{*}A| consisting of elements containing the fiber f−1​zf^{-1}{z}. Then VzV_{z} is base point free outside the fiber f−1​zf^{-1}z as AA is very ample. M=1p​(M1+⋯+Mp⁡(d+1)).M=\frac{1}{p}(M_{1}+\cdots+M_{p(d+1)}).

Then (X,Γ+M)(X,\Gamma+M) is ϵ\epsilon-lc outside f−1​zf^{-1}z and is not lc at any point of f−1​zf^{-1}z by [Ko+92, Theorem 18.22].

Let ϵ′=12​min⁡{e,ϵ}\epsilon^{\prime}=\frac{1}{2}\min\{e,\epsilon\} and let uu be the largest number such that (X,Γ+u​M)(X,\Gamma+uM) is ϵ′\epsilon^{\prime}-lc. Replacing ϵ\epsilon with ϵ′\epsilon^{\prime} and replacing Γ\Gamma with Γ+u​M\Gamma+uM (and replacing A,rA,r with (d+2)​A(d+2)A, (d+2)d​r(d+2)^{d}r respectively), we can assume that ϵ≤e\epsilon\leq e and that there exists a prime divisor TT over XX mapped to zz with a⁡(T,X,Γ)=ϵa(T,X,\Gamma)=\epsilon.

Let π:X^→X\pi:\hat{X}\to X be a ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorialisation extracting TT but no other divisors (if TT is not exceptional over XX, then π\pi is a small ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorialisation). Write KX^+Γ^=π∗​(KX+Γ)K_{\hat{X}}+\hat{\Gamma}=\pi^{*}(K_{X}+\Gamma). Let Θ^\hat{\Theta} be the same as π∗​B\pi^{*}B except that we replace the coefficient of TT by 1. Then the coefficients of Θ^\hat{\Theta} are in ℜ\mathfrak{R} (we may suppose that 1∈ℜ1\in\mathfrak{R}). By construction, Γ^−Θ^≥−ϵ​T\hat{\Gamma}-\hat{\Theta}\geq-\epsilon T, so

n⁡(KX+Λ)∼(n+2)​l​f∗​A.n(K_{X}+\Lambda)\sim(n+2)lf^{*}A.

The following theorem is similar to [Bi22, Theorem 1.7] but with three differences. First, we add the assumption that Conjecture 1.3 holds. Second, we remove the condition that −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is big over ZZ. Third, we make nn independent of rr. The notation is also slightly different; B,ΓB,\Gamma in the following theorem correspond to Δ,B\Delta,B in [Bi22, Theorem 1.7] respectively. We follow the arguments in the proofs of [Bi22, Theorem 1.7 and Proposition 4.16] with some modifications.

Theorem 4.4.

Assume Conjecture 1.3 holds when dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell for some natural number ℓ\ell. Let d,rd,r be natural numbers, ϵ\epsilon be a positive real number and ℜ⊂[0,1]\mathfrak{R}\subset[0,1] be a finite set of rational numbers. Then there exist a natural number nn depending on d,ϵ,ℜd,\epsilon,\mathfrak{R} and a natural number mm depending on d,r,ϵ,ℜd,r,\epsilon,\mathfrak{R} satisfying the following (note that nn is independent of rr). Assume that

  • •

    (X,Γ)→Z,A(X,\Gamma)\to Z,A is a (d,r,ϵ)(d,r,\epsilon)-Fano type fibration with dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell, and

  • •

    (X,B)(X,B) is a pair such that B≤ΓB\leq\Gamma and the coefficients of BB are in ℜ\mathfrak{R}.

Then there is a ℚ\mathbb{Q}-divisor Λ\Lambda on XX such that

  • •

    Λ≥B\Lambda\geq B,

  • •

    (X,Λ)(X,\Lambda) is klt, and

  • •

    n⁡(KX+Λ)∼m​f∗​An(K_{X}+\Lambda)\sim mf^{*}A.

Proof.

Step 1. When dimZ=0\dim Z=0, (X,B)(X,B) is log bounded by [Bi21, Corollary 1.4]. Applying [Bi19, Lemma 2.4], the Cartier index of KX+BK_{X}+B depends only on d,ϵ,ℜd,\epsilon,\mathfrak{R}. By the effective base point freeness [Ko93], there is a natural number nn depending only on d,ϵ,ℜd,\epsilon,\mathfrak{R} such that −n⁡(KX+B)-n(K_{X}+B) is base point free. Let Λ=B+R\Lambda=B+R where n​RnR is a general element of |−n⁡(KX+B)||-n(K_{X}+B)|. Then n⁡(KX+Λ)∼0n(K_{X}+\Lambda)\sim 0 and (X,Λ)(X,\Lambda) is klt. So we may suppose that dimZ>0\dim Z>0.

Step 2. It suffices to show that, for any closed point z∈Zz\in Z, there is a boundary Λ≥B\Lambda\geq B such that (X,Λ)(X,\Lambda) is klt over some neighbourhood UzU_{z} of zz and n⁡(KX+Λ)∼m​f∗​An(K_{X}+\Lambda)\sim mf^{*}A, where nn only depends on d,ϵ,ℜd,\epsilon,\mathfrak{R} and mm only depends on d,r,ϵ,ℜd,r,\epsilon,\mathfrak{R}. Indeed, if this is true, we can find finitely many closed points z1,⋯,zkz_{1},\cdots,z_{k} in ZZ such that the corresponding open sets UziU_{z_{i}} cover ZZ. For each ziz_{i}, let Λi\Lambda_{i} be the corresponding boundary as above. Then

n⁡(Λi−B)∈|m​f∗​A−n⁡(KX+B)|.n(\Lambda_{i}-B)\in|mf^{*}A-n(K_{X}+B)|.

Therefore, if we let Λ=B+R\Lambda=B+R where n​RnR is a general element of |m​f∗​A−n⁡(KX+B)||mf^{*}A-n(K_{X}+B)|, then n⁡(KX+Λ)∼m​f∗​An(K_{X}+\Lambda)\sim mf^{*}A and (X,Λ)(X,\Lambda) is klt over each UziU_{z_{i}}. As the open sets UziU_{z_{i}} cover XX, it follows that (X,Λ)(X,\Lambda) is klt everywhere and we are done. From now on we fix a closed point z∈Zz\in Z.

Lemma 4.5.

Let f:X→Zf:X\to Z be a contraction such that XX is of Fano type over ZZ and XX is ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorial. Let (X,B)(X,B) be an ϵ\epsilon-lc pair with 0<ϵ<10<\epsilon<1 such that −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ and the coefficients of BB are in a set ℜ\mathfrak{R} of rational numbers. Then there exist a pair (X¯,B¯)(\bar{X},\bar{B}) and a contraction f¯:X¯→Z¯\bar{f}:\bar{X}\to\bar{Z} such that

  • •

    X¯,Z¯\bar{X},\bar{Z} are projective,

  • •

    X¯\bar{X} is ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorial,

  • •

    X¯\bar{X} is of Fano type over Z¯\bar{Z}

  • •

    (X¯,B¯)(\bar{X},\bar{B}) is ϵ\epsilon-lc,

  • •

    the coefficients of B¯\bar{B} are in ℜ\mathfrak{R},

  • •

    −(KX¯+B¯)-(K_{\bar{X}}+\bar{B}) is nef over Z¯\bar{Z},

  • •

    ZZ is an open subset of Z¯\bar{Z}, and

  • •

    (X,B)=(X¯,B¯)×Z¯Z(X,B)=(\bar{X},\bar{B})\times_{\bar{Z}}Z.

Proof.

As XX is of Fano type over ZZ and as −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ, −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is semi-ample over ZZ. Thus there is a ℚ\mathbb{Q}-boundary Γ≥B\Gamma\geq B such that (X,Γ)(X,\Gamma) is ϵ\epsilon-lc and KX+Γ∼ℚ0/ZK_{X}+\Gamma\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}0/Z.

Since X,ZX,Z are assumed to be quasi-projective, we can find compactifications X⊂XcX\subset X^{c} and Z⊂ZcZ\subset Z^{c} such that Xc,ZcX^{c},Z^{c} are projective and the morphism f:X→Zf:X\to Z can be extended to fc:Xc→Zcf^{c}:X^{c}\to Z^{c}. Let Γc\Gamma^{c} be the closure of Γ\Gamma in XcX^{c} and let πc:Wc→Xc\pi^{c}:W^{c}\to X^{c} be a log resolution of (Xc,Γc∪(fc)−1​(Zc∖Z))(X^{c},\Gamma^{c}\cup(f^{c})^{-1}(Z^{c}\setminus Z)). Denote W=(πc)−1​(X)W=(\pi^{c})^{-1}(X) and π=πc∣W\pi=\pi^{c}\mid_{W}. Write

KW+ΓW−FW=π∗​(KX+Γ)K_{W}+\Gamma_{W}-F_{W}=\pi^{*}(K_{X}+\Gamma)

where ΓW,FW\Gamma_{W},F_{W} are effective ℚ\mathbb{Q}-divisors without common components. Let ΓWc\Gamma_{W}^{c} be the closure of ΓW\Gamma_{W} in WcW^{c}. Then (Wc,ΓWc)(W^{c},\Gamma_{W}^{c}) is an ϵ\epsilon-lc pair. By [BCHM], (Wc,ΓWc)(W^{c},\Gamma_{W}^{c}) has a log canonical model over XcX^{c}, which we denote by (X^,Γ^)(\hat{X},\hat{\Gamma}). Then (X^,Γ^)(\hat{X},\hat{\Gamma}) is an ϵ\epsilon-lc pair and (X^,Γ^)×ZcZ=(X,Γ)(\hat{X},\hat{\Gamma})\times_{Z^{c}}Z=(X,\Gamma). Let X~\widetilde{X} be a small ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorialization of X^\hat{X}. Since XX is ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorial, we have X~×ZcZ=X\widetilde{X}\times_{Z^{c}}Z=X. Replacing X^\hat{X} with X~\widetilde{X}, we may assume that X^\hat{X} is ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorial.

By [Bi12, Theorem 5.2], we can run an MMP on KX^+Γ^K_{\hat{X}}+\hat{\Gamma} over ZcZ^{c} and the MMP ends with a good minimal model over ZcZ^{c}, which we denote by (X¯,Γ¯)(\bar{X},\bar{\Gamma}). Then KX¯+Γ¯K_{\bar{X}}+\bar{\Gamma} is semi-ample over ZcZ^{c}. Moreover, (X¯,Γ¯)(\bar{X},\bar{\Gamma}) is ϵ\epsilon-lc and (X¯,Γ¯)×ZcZ=(X,Γ)(\bar{X},\bar{\Gamma})\times_{Z^{c}}Z=(X,\Gamma). Let f¯:X¯→Z¯/Zc\bar{f}:\bar{X}\to\bar{Z}/Z^{c} be the contraction induced by KX¯+Γ¯K_{\bar{X}}+\bar{\Gamma} over ZcZ^{c}. Then Z¯×ZcZ=Z\bar{Z}\times_{Z^{c}}Z=Z and the restriction of f¯\bar{f} over ZZ coincides with f:X→Zf:X\to Z. By now we have constructed a contraction X¯→Z¯\bar{X}\to\bar{Z} between projective varieties and an ϵ\epsilon-lc pair (X¯,Γ¯)(\bar{X},\bar{\Gamma}) such that X¯\bar{X} is ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorial, ZZ is an open subset of Z¯\bar{Z}, KX¯+Γ¯∼ℚ0/Z¯K_{\bar{X}}+\bar{\Gamma}\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}0/\bar{Z} and (X¯,Γ¯)×Z¯Z=(X,Γ)(\bar{X},\bar{\Gamma})\times_{\bar{Z}}Z=(X,\Gamma). As −KX-K_{X} is big over ZZ, −KX¯-K_{\bar{X}} is also big over Z¯\bar{Z}, which implies that X¯\bar{X} is of Fano type over Z¯\bar{Z}.

Denote by B¯\bar{B} the closure of BB in X¯\bar{X}. Then the coefficients of B¯\bar{B} are in ℜ\mathfrak{R} and B¯≤Γ¯\bar{B}\leq\bar{\Gamma}. Theorem 4.6.

Assume Conjecture 1.3 holds when dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell for some natural number ℓ\ell. Let dd be a natural number, ϵ\epsilon be a positive real number and ℜ⊂[0,1]\mathfrak{R}\subset[0,1] be a finite set of rational numbers. Then there is a natural number nn depending only on d,ϵ,ℜd,\epsilon,\mathfrak{R} satisfying the following. Assume (X,B)(X,B) is a pair and X→ZX\to Z is a contraction such that

  • •

    (X,B)(X,B) is ϵ\epsilon-lc of dimension dd and dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell,

  • •

    the coefficients of BB are in ℜ\mathfrak{R},

  • •

    XX is of Fano type over ZZ, and

  • •

    −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ.

Then there is a ℚ\mathbb{Q}-divisor Λ\Lambda on XX such that

  • •

    Λ≥B\Lambda\geq B,

  • •

    (X,Λ)(X,\Lambda) is klt, and

  • •

    n⁡(KX+Λ)∼0/Zn(K_{X}+\Lambda)\sim 0/Z.

Proof.

We may assume that ϵ<1\epsilon<1. Taking a small ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorialization, we may assume that XX is ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorial. Applying Lemma 4.5, we can assume that X,ZX,Z are projective. As XX is of Fano type over ZZ and as −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ, −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is semi-ample over ZZ. Thus there is a ℚ\mathbb{Q}-boundary Γ≥B\Gamma\geq B such that (X,Γ)(X,\Gamma) is ϵ\epsilon-lc and KX+Γ∼ℚ0/ZK_{X}+\Gamma\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}0/Z. That is, KX+Γ∼ℚf∗LK_{X}+\Gamma\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}f^{*}L for some ℚ\mathbb{Q}-Cartier ℚ\mathbb{Q}-divisor LL on ZZ. Let AA be a very ample divisor on ZZ such that A−LA-L is ample and denote r=AdimZr=A^{\dim Z} (note that rr may not depend on d,ϵ,ℜd,\epsilon,\mathfrak{R}). Then f:(X,Γ)→Z,Af:(X,\Gamma)\to Z,A is a (d,r,ϵ)(d,r,\epsilon)-Fano type fibration. By Theorem 4.4, there is n∈ℕn\in\mathbb{N} depending on d,ϵ,ℜd,\epsilon,\mathfrak{R} and m∈ℕm\in\mathbb{N} depending on d,r,ϵ,ℜd,r,\epsilon,\mathfrak{R} and there is a boundary Λ≥B\Lambda\geq B such that (X,Λ)(X,\Lambda) is klt and n⁡(KX+Λ)∼m​f∗​An(K_{X}+\Lambda)\sim mf^{*}A. Thus n⁡(KX+Λ)∼0/Zn(K_{X}+\Lambda)\sim 0/Z. ∎

Corollary 4.7.

Assume Conjecture 1.3 holds when dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell for some natural number ℓ\ell. Then Conjecture 1.1 holds when dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell.

Proof.

It follows from Theorem 4.6 directly. ∎

5. Proof of (2) ⇒\Rightarrow (4) in Theorem 1.6

Proposition 5.1.

Assume Conjecture 1.1 holds when X→ZX\to Z is birational, B=0B=0 and dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell for some natural number ℓ\ell. Then Conjecture 1.3 holds when X→ZX\to Z is birational, B=0B=0 and dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell.

Proof.

Let f:X→Zf:X\to Z be a birational contraction with dimX=d\dim X=d and dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell such that XX is of Fano type over ZZ, XX is ϵ\epsilon-lc and −KX-K_{X} is nef over ZZ. Let z∈Zz\in Z be a closed point. By the assumption that Conjecture 1.1 holds in this special case, there is a natural number nn depending only on d,ϵd,\epsilon such that, after shrinking ZZ around zz there is a boundary ΛX\Lambda_{X} on XX such that (X,ΛX)(X,\Lambda_{X}) is klt and n⁡(KX+ΛX)∼0/Zn(K_{X}+\Lambda_{X})\sim 0/Z. Let Λ\Lambda be the pushdown of ΛX\Lambda_{X} on ZZ. Then (Z,Λ)(Z,\Lambda) is klt and n⁡(KZ+Λ)n(K_{Z}+\Lambda) is Cartier. It suffices to show that there are t>0t>0 depending only on d,ϵd,\epsilon and an effective Cartier divisor HH on a neighbourhood of z∈Zz\in Z such that z∈Supp⁡Hz\in\Supp H and (Z,Λ+t​H)(Z,\Lambda+tH) is lc near zz. Indeed, if (Z,Λ+t​H)(Z,\Lambda+tH) is lc near zz, (X,ΛX+t​f∗​H)(X,\Lambda_{X}+tf^{*}H) is lc over zz, which implies that (X,t​f∗​H)(X,tf^{*}H) is so.

Let π:Y→Z\pi:Y\to Z be a plt blow-up of (Z∋z,Λ)(Z\ni z,\Lambda) with the exceptional divisor EE (its existence is guaranteed by Lemma 2.27). Then (Y,E+ΛY)(Y,E+\Lambda_{Y}) is plt and −E-E is ample over ZZ, where ΛY\Lambda_{Y} is the birational transform of Λ\Lambda on YY. Then

KY+E+ΛY=π∗​(KZ+Λ)+a⁡(E,Z,Λ)⋅E,K_{Y}+E+\Lambda_{Y}=\pi^{*}(K_{Z}+\Lambda)+a(E,Z,\Lambda)\cdot E,

which implies that −(KY+E+ΛY)-(K_{Y}+E+\Lambda_{Y}) is ample over ZZ. We claim that YY is of Fano type over ZZ. Indeed, (Y,(1−e)​E+ΛY)(Y,(1-e)E+\Lambda_{Y}) is klt and −(KY+(1−e)​E+ΛY)-(K_{Y}+(1-e)E+\Lambda_{Y}) is ample over ZZ for a sufficiently small e>0e>0. Moreover, n⁡(E+ΛY)n(E+\Lambda_{Y}) is an integral divisor. By the boundedness of lc complements [Bi19, Theorem 1.8], there is a natural number mm depending only on d,nd,n such that, after shrinking ZZ around zz there is a boundary ΩY≥E+ΛY\Omega_{Y}\geq E+\Lambda_{Y} on YY such that (Y,ΩY)(Y,\Omega_{Y}) is lc and m⁡(KY+ΩY)∼0/Zm(K_{Y}+\Omega_{Y})\sim 0/Z. Let Ω\Omega be the pushdown of ΩY\Omega_{Y} on ZZ. By construction, we have (Z,Ω)(Z,\Omega) is lc, m⁡(KZ+Ω)m(K_{Z}+\Omega) is Cartier, Ω≥Λ\Omega\geq\Lambda, and (Z,Ω)(Z,\Omega) is not klt near zz. Thus z∈Supp⁡(Ω−Λ)z\in\Supp(\Omega-\Lambda). Let H=m​n​(Ω−Λ)H=mn(\Omega-\Lambda) and t=1m​nt=\frac{1}{mn}, then HH is Cartier and (Z,Λ+t​H)(Z,\Lambda+tH) is lc. ∎

6. Proof of (4) ⇒\Rightarrow (5) in Theorem 1.6

Proposition 6.1.

Assume that Conjecture 1.3 holds when X→ZX\to Z is birational, B=0B=0 and dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell for some natural number ℓ\ell. Then Conjecture 1.4 holds when dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell.

Proof.

Let (Z,Δ)(Z,\Delta) be an ϵ\epsilon-lc pair with a closed point z∈Zz\in Z. We may assume that ϵ<1\epsilon<1. Denote by 𝔪z\mathfrak{m}_{z} the ideal sheaf of z∈Zz\in Z. Let tt be largest number such that the triple (Z,Δ,𝔪zt)(Z,\Delta,\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t}) is ϵ2\frac{\epsilon}{2}-lc. By Corollary 2.19, it suffices to show that tt is bounded from below by a positive constant depending only on dimZ,ϵ\dim Z,\epsilon. If t>1−ϵt>1-\epsilon, we are done. So we may assume that t≤1−ϵt\leq 1-\epsilon.

There exists a prime divisor TT over ZZ such that

a⁡(T,Z,Δ,𝔪zt)=ϵ2.a(T,Z,\Delta,\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t})=\frac{\epsilon}{2}.

Since (Z,Δ)(Z,\Delta) is ϵ\epsilon-lc, we have

t⋅μT​𝔪z≥ϵ2.t\cdot\mu_{T}\mathfrak{m}_{z}\geq\frac{\epsilon}{2}.

So it suffices to show that μT​𝔪z\mu_{T}\mathfrak{m}_{z} is bounded from above by a constant depending only on dimZ,ϵ\dim Z,\epsilon.

Let f:X→Zf:X\to Z be a ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorialisation extracting TT but no other divisors (if TT is not exceptional over ZZ, then ff is a small ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorialisation). As (Z,Δ,𝔪zt)(Z,\Delta,\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t}) is ϵ2\frac{\epsilon}{2}-lc and as a⁡(T,Z,Δ,𝔪zt)=ϵ2a(T,Z,\Delta,\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t})=\frac{\epsilon}{2}, by Lemma 2.17 and Remark 2.18, there exists an effective Cartier divisor DD on ZZ such that z∈Supp⁡Dz\in\Supp D, (Z,Δ+t​D)(Z,\Delta+tD) is ϵ2\frac{\epsilon}{2}-lc and

a⁡(T,Z,Δ+t​D)=ϵ2.a(T,Z,\Delta+tD)=\frac{\epsilon}{2}.

Let KX+ΓK_{X}+\Gamma be the pullback of KZ+Δ+t​DK_{Z}+\Delta+tD to XX. Then Γ\Gamma is effective as μT​Γ=ϵ2≥0\mu_{T}\Gamma=\frac{\epsilon}{2}\geq 0. Moreover, (X,Γ)(X,\Gamma) is ϵ2\frac{\epsilon}{2}-lc and KX+Γ∼ℝ0/ZK_{X}+\Gamma\sim_{\mathbb{R}}0/Z. Hence XX is of Fano type over ZZ.

Run an MMP on −KX-K_{X} over ZZ and let X′X^{\prime} be the resulting model with the induced morphism f′:X′→Zf^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to Z. Then −KX′-K_{X^{\prime}} is nef over ZZ. As (X,Γ)(X,\Gamma) is ϵ2\frac{\epsilon}{2}-lc and as KX+Γ∼ℝ0/ZK_{X}+\Gamma\sim_{\mathbb{R}}0/Z, (X′,Γ′)(X^{\prime},\Gamma^{\prime}) is also ϵ2\frac{\epsilon}{2}-lc, where Γ′\Gamma^{\prime} is the pushdown of Γ\Gamma to X′X^{\prime}. Thus X′X^{\prime} is ϵ2\frac{\epsilon}{2}-lc. By assumption Conjecture 1.3 holds for X′→ZX^{\prime}\to Z, that is, there are a positive number uu depending on dimZ,ϵ\dim Z,\epsilon and an effective Cartier divisor FF on some neighbourhood of z∈Zz\in Z such that z∈Supp⁡Fz\in\Supp F and (X′,u⋅f′⁣∗​F)(X^{\prime},u\cdot f^{\prime*}F) is lc over zz. Then (X,u⋅f∗​F)(X,u\cdot f^{*}F) is lc over zz, as X⇢X′X\dashrightarrow X^{\prime} is an MMP on −KX-K_{X}. Thus

μT​𝔪z≤μT​f∗​F≤1u,\mu_{T}\mathfrak{m}_{z}\leq\mu_{T}f^{*}F\leq\frac{1}{u},

where uu only depends on dimZ,ϵ\dim Z,\epsilon. ∎

Proof of Theorem 1.6.

It follows from Proposition 3.3, 5.1, 6.1 and Corollary 4.7. ∎

7. The surface case

The goal of this section is to prove Conjecture 1.4 in dimension 2. We begin with some properties of klt germs.

Lemma 7.1.

[KM98, Theorem 5.22] A klt germ Z∋zZ\ni z is a rational singularity.

Lemma 7.2.

[Ma02, Theorem 4-6-18(iii)] A klt germ Z∋zZ\ni z of dimension 2 is analytically isomorphic to (ℂ2∋0)/G(\mathbb{C}^{2}\ni 0)/G, where G⊂G​L​(2,ℂ)G\subset GL(2,\mathbb{C}) is a finite subgroup.

Proposition 7.3.

Let Z∋zZ\ni z be a klt germ of dimension 2 and let π:Y→Z\pi:Y\to Z be the minimal resolution with the exceptional divisor EE. Denote by CfC_{f} the fundamental cycle of the singularity Z∋zZ\ni z on YY. Then Cf≤6​EC_{f}\leq 6E.

Proof.

Note that the fundamental cycle depends only on the analytic isomorphism class of the singularity, as it is determined by the intersection matrix of components of the exceptional divisor. The proposition follows from Lemma 7.2 and Proposition A.1 in the appendix. ∎

Lemma 7.4.

Let (Z,Δ)(Z,\Delta) be a pair of dimension 2 with a closed point z∈Zz\in Z such that mld⁡(Z∋z,Δ)>0\mld(Z\ni z,\Delta)>0. Then KZK_{Z} is ℚ\mathbb{Q}-Cartier near zz and ZZ is klt near zz.

Proof.

Let π:W→Z\pi:W\to Z be the minimal resolution. Shrinking ZZ we may assume that π\pi is an isomorphism outside zz. Write

KW+ΔW+EW=π∗​(KZ+Δ)K_{W}+\Delta_{W}+E_{W}=\pi^{*}(K_{Z}+\Delta)

where ΔW\Delta_{W} is the birational transform of Δ\Delta and EWE_{W} is exceptional over ZZ.

We claim that (W,EW)(W,E_{W}) is klt over zz. Indeed, for any prime divisor DD over WW with π⁡(centerW⁡D)=z\pi(\cent_{W}D)=z, we have

a⁡(D,W,EW)≥a⁡(D,W,ΔW+EW)=a⁡(D,Z,Δ)>0;a(D,W,E_{W})\geq a(D,W,\Delta_{W}+E_{W})=a(D,Z,\Delta)>0;

for any prime divisor DD over WW so that π⁡(centerW⁡D)\pi(\cent_{W}D) contains zz but is not zz, we have

a⁡(D,W,EW)=1a(D,W,E_{W})=1

because DD is a prime divisor on WW which is not exceptional over ZZ. Thus (W,EW)(W,E_{W}) is klt over zz. Shrinking ZZ around zz, we may suppose that (W,EW)(W,E_{W}) is klt everywhere.

For any exceptional/Z/Z prime divisor TT on WW, we have

−(KW+EW)⋅T=ΔW⋅T≥0.-(K_{W}+E_{W})\cdot T=\Delta_{W}\cdot T\geq 0.

So −(KW+EW)-(K_{W}+E_{W}) is big and nef over ZZ. Therefore, WW is of Fano type over ZZ.

Denote by T1,⋯,TkT_{1},\cdots,T_{k} all the exceptional/Z/Z prime divisors on WW. Then the intersection matrix (Ti⋅Tj)(T_{i}\cdot T_{j}) is negative definite. So there are rational numbers a1,⋯,aka_{1},\cdots,a_{k} such that

(KW+TW)⋅Tj=0 where ​TW=∑i=1kai​Ti,(K_{W}+T_{W})\cdot T_{j}=0\quad\text{ where }T_{W}=\sum_{i=1}^{k}a_{i}T_{i},

for j=1,⋯,kj=1,\cdots,k. Hence KW+TW≡0/ZK_{W}+T_{W}\equiv 0/Z, which implies that KW+TW∼ℚ0/ZK_{W}+T_{W}\sim_{\mathbb{Q}}0/Z as WW is of Fano type over ZZ. Thus KZK_{Z} is ℚ\mathbb{Q}-Cartier as it is the pushdown of KW+TWK_{W}+T_{W} to ZZ.

Finally we show that ZZ is klt. Since WW is of Fano type over ZZ, there is a klt pair (W,ΓW)(W,\Gamma_{W}) such that KW+ΓW∼ℝ0/ZK_{W}+\Gamma_{W}\sim_{\mathbb{R}}0/Z. Let Γ\Gamma be the pushdown of ΓW\Gamma_{W} to ZZ. Then (Z,Γ)(Z,\Gamma) is klt, which implies that ZZ is klt. ∎

We need the following result in [Ch22] on the lower bound of the lc threshold of a smooth curve with respect to a pair on a smooth surface.

Lemma 7.5.

[Ch22, Theorem 1.9] Let ZZ be a smooth surface with a closed point z∈Zz\in Z and let (Z,Δ)(Z,\Delta) be a pair such that mld⁡(Z∋z,Δ)≥ϵ\mld(Z\ni z,\Delta)\geq\epsilon with 0<ϵ≤10<\epsilon\leq 1. Let HH be a smooth curve on ZZ passing zz such that μH​Δ≤1−ϵ\mu_{H}\Delta\leq 1-\epsilon and (Δ′⋅H)z≤2(\Delta^{\prime}\cdot H)_{z}\leq 2, where Δ′=Δ−μH​Δ⋅H\Delta^{\prime}=\Delta-\mu_{H}\Delta\cdot H. Then (Z,Δ+ϵ22​H)(Z,\Delta+\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2}H) is lc near zz.

Proof of Theorem 1.7.

Case 1: z∈Zz\in Z is a smooth point. Since (Z,Δ)(Z,\Delta) is lc near zz, the multiplicity of Δ\Delta at zz is at most 2. Hence there is a smooth curve HH on some neighbourhood of z∈Zz\in Z such that z∈Hz\in H, H⊄Supp⁡ΔH\not\subset\Supp\Delta and (Δ⋅H)z≤2(\Delta\cdot H)_{z}\leq 2. Applying Lemma 7.5, we deduce that (Z,Δ+ϵ22​H)(Z,\Delta+\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2}H) is lc near zz.

Case 2: z∈Zz\in Z is not a smooth point. Let π:W→Z\pi:W\to Z be the minimal resolution and denote by EE the exceptional divisor on WW over Z∋zZ\ni z. Let KW+ΔWK_{W}+\Delta_{W} be the pullback of KZ+ΔK_{Z}+\Delta to WW. Then ΔW≥0\Delta_{W}\geq 0 as π\pi is the minimal resolution.

By Corollary 2.19, it suffices to show that (W,ΔW,π∗​𝔪zt)(W,\Delta_{W},\pi^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t}) is lc over zz, where t=ϵ2/24t=\epsilon^{2}/24 and 𝔪z\mathfrak{m}_{z} is the ideal sheaf of z∈Zz\in Z. By Lemma 7.4, Z∋zZ\ni z is a klt germ and hence is a rational singularity by Lemma 7.1. It follows from Lemma 2.21 that EE is a simple normal crossing divisor on WW. By Lemma 2.25,

π∗​𝔪z=𝒪W​(−Cf)\pi^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}=\mathcal{O}_{W}(-C_{f})

where CfC_{f} is the fundamental cycle of the singularity Z∋zZ\ni z on WW. Note that Cf≤6​EC_{f}\leq 6E by Proposition 7.3, so it suffices to show that (W,ΔW+ϵ24​E)(W,\Delta_{W}+\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{4}E) is lc near EE.

Let DD be an irreducible component of EE. Then DD is a smooth rational curve by Lemma 2.21, which implies that (KW+D)⋅D=−2(K_{W}+D)\cdot D=-2. Since (KW+ΔW)⋅D=0(K_{W}+\Delta_{W})\cdot D=0, we have

(ΔW−D)⋅D=2.(\Delta_{W}-D)\cdot D=2.

Denote a=μD​ΔWa=\mu_{D}\Delta_{W}. Then a≤1−ϵ<1a\leq 1-\epsilon<1 as mld⁡(Z∋z,Δ)≥ϵ\mld(Z\ni z,\Delta)\geq\epsilon. Note that D⋅D<0D\cdot D<0, we have

(ΔW−a​D)⋅D<2.(\Delta_{W}-aD)\cdot D<2.

Applying Lemma 7.5, we deduce that (W,ΔW+ϵ22​D)(W,\Delta_{W}+\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2}D) is lc near DD.

It suffices to show that (W,ΔW+ϵ24​E)(W,\Delta_{W}+\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{4}E) is lc near pp for any closed point p∈Ep\in E. If pp is not the intersection point of two components of EE, by the above argument, (W,ΔW+ϵ22​E)(W,\Delta_{W}+\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2}E) is lc near pp. Otherwise, pp is the intersection point of two components D,FD,F of EE, then E=D+FE=D+F near pp. By the above argument, (W,ΔW+ϵ22​D)(W,\Delta_{W}+\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2}D) and (W,ΔW+ϵ22​F)(W,\Delta_{W}+\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{2}F) are lc near pp, which implies that

(W,ΔW+ϵ24​(D+F))\big(W,\Delta_{W}+\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{4}(D+F)\big)

is lc near pp. Therefore, (W,ΔW+ϵ24​E)(W,\Delta_{W}+\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{4}E) is lc near pp. ∎

Proof of Corollary 1.8.

When dimZ=1\dim Z=1, Conjecture 1.4 holds obviously. When dimZ=2\dim Z=2, Conjecture 1.4 follows from Theorem 1.7 directly. By Theorem 1.6, Conjecture 1.1 and 1.3 hold when dimZ≤2\dim Z\leq 2. ∎

8. The toric case

The goal of this section is to prove Conjecture 1.3 and 1.4 in the toric case. First we recall a result of Ambro [Am22, Theorem 3.12]. Note that the condition in [Am22, Theorem 3.12] that −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is semi-ample over ZZ is equivalent to that −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ, because XX is of Fano type over ZZ as X→ZX\to Z is a toric contraction.

Lemma 8.1.

[Am22, Theorem 3.12] Let dd be a natural number and 𝔄⊂[0,1]\mathfrak{A}\subset[0,1] be an ACC set. Then there is a positive real number tt depending only on d,𝔄d,\mathfrak{A} satisfying the following. Assume (X,B)(X,B) is a toric pair, ZZ is an affine toric variety with dimZ>0\dim Z>0, f:X→Zf:X\to Z is a toric contraction and z∈Zz\in Z is a torus invariant closed point such that

  • •

    mld(X/Z∋z,B)≥ϵ\mld(X/Z\ni z,B)\geq\epsilon for some ϵ>0\epsilon>0,

  • •

    B=∑i(1−ai)​BiB=\sum_{i}(1-a_{i})B_{i} with aiϵ∈𝔄\frac{a_{i}}{\epsilon}\in\mathfrak{A}, where the BiB_{i} are distinct toric prime divisors,

  • •

    −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ.

Then there exists an effective toric Cartier divisor HH on ZZ such that z∈Supp⁡Hz\in\Supp H and (X,B+γ​f∗​H)(X,B+\gamma f^{*}H) is lc over zz, where γ=ϵ⋅t\gamma=\epsilon\cdot t.

The following lemma is a direct consequence of Lemma 8.1, which asserts that Conjecture 1.3 holds in the toric case when the coefficients of BB belong to a fixed DCC set.

Lemma 8.2.

Let dd be a natural number, ϵ\epsilon be a positive real number and 𝔇⊂[0,1]\mathfrak{D}\subset[0,1] be a DCC set. Then there is a positive number tt depending only on d,ϵ,𝔇d,\epsilon,\mathfrak{D} satisfying the following. Assume (X,B)(X,B) is a toric pair, ZZ is an affine toric variety with dimZ>0\dim Z>0, f:X→Zf:X\to Z is a toric contraction and z∈Zz\in Z is a torus invariant closed point such that

  • •

    mld(X/Z∋z,B)≥ϵ\mld(X/Z\ni z,B)\geq\epsilon,

  • •

    the coefficients of BB are in 𝔇\mathfrak{D}, and

  • •

    −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ.

Then there exists an effective toric Cartier divisor HH on ZZ such that z∈Supp⁡Hz\in\Supp H and (X,B+t​f∗​H)(X,B+tf^{*}H) is lc over zz.

Proof.

It follows from Lemma 8.1 by taking 𝔄=(1−𝔇)/ϵ\mathfrak{A}=(1-\mathfrak{D})/\epsilon. ∎

In the following theorem, we remove the condition on the coefficients of BB in Lemma 8.2, so Conjecture 1.3 holds in the toric case. The argument of its proof is similar to that of Proposition 6.1 and the case that B=0B=0 is known by [Am22, Theorem 3.12].

Theorem 8.3.

Let dd be a natural number, ϵ\epsilon be a positive real number. Then there is a positive number tt depending only on d,ϵd,\epsilon satisfying the following. Assume (X,B)(X,B) is a toric pair, f:X→Zf:X\to Z is a toric contraction with dimZ>0\dim Z>0 and z∈Zz\in Z is a torus invariant closed point such that

  • •

    mld(X/Z∋z,B)≥ϵ\mld(X/Z\ni z,B)\geq\epsilon, and

  • •

    −(KX+B)-(K_{X}+B) is nef over ZZ.

Then there exists an effective Cartier divisor HH on a neighbourhood of z∈Zz\in Z such that z∈Supp⁡Hz\in\Supp H and (X,B+t​f∗​H)(X,B+tf^{*}H) is lc over zz.

Proof.

Let tt be the largest number such that

mld(X/Z∋z,B,f∗𝔪zt)≥ϵ2,\mld(X/Z\ni z,B,f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t})\geq\frac{\epsilon}{2},

where 𝔪z\mathfrak{m}_{z} is the ideal sheaf of the closed point z∈Zz\in Z. By Corollary 2.19, it suffices to show that tt is bounded from below by a positive constant depending only on d,ϵd,\epsilon. If t>1t>1, we are done. So we may suppose that t≤1t\leq 1.

We can find a toric prime divisor TT over X/Z∋zX/Z\ni z so that

a⁡(T,X,B,f∗​𝔪zt)=ϵ2.a(T,X,B,f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t})=\frac{\epsilon}{2}.

Since mld(X/Z∋z,B)≥ϵ\mld(X/Z\ni z,B)\geq\epsilon, we have

t⋅μT​f∗​𝔪z≥ϵ2.t\cdot\mu_{T}f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}\geq\frac{\epsilon}{2}.

So it suffices to show that μT​f∗​𝔪z\mu_{T}f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z} is bounded from above by a constant depending only on d,ϵd,\epsilon.

Let π:Y→X\pi:Y\to X be a toric ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorialisation extracting TT but no other divisors (if TT is not exceptional over XX, then π\pi is a small toric ℚ\mathbb{Q}-factorialisation). By Lemma 2.17 and Remark 2.18, there exists an effective Cartier divisor DD on ZZ such that z∈Supp⁡Dz\in\Supp D,

a⁡(T,X,B+t​f∗​D)=a⁡(T,X,B,f∗​𝔪zt)=ϵ2a(T,X,B+tf^{*}D)=a(T,X,B,f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t})=\frac{\epsilon}{2}

and

mld(X/Z∋z,B+tf∗D)=mld(X/Z∋z,B,f∗𝔪zt)=ϵ2.\mld(X/Z\ni z,B+tf^{*}D)=\mld(X/Z\ni z,B,f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z}^{t})=\frac{\epsilon}{2}.

Let KY+ΩK_{Y}+\Omega be the pullback of KX+B+t​f∗​DK_{X}+B+tf^{*}D to YY. Then Ω\Omega is effective as μT​Ω=ϵ2≥0\mu_{T}\Omega=\frac{\epsilon}{2}\geq 0. Moreover, −(KY+Ω)-(K_{Y}+\Omega) is nef over ZZ and

mld(Y/Z∋z,Ω)=ϵ2.\mld(Y/Z\ni z,\Omega)=\frac{\epsilon}{2}.

As Y→ZY\to Z is a toric contraction, YY is of Fano type over ZZ. So −(KY+Ω)-(K_{Y}+\Omega) is semi-ample over ZZ. It follows that there exists an effective ℝ\mathbb{R}-divisor RR on YY such that KY+Ω+R∼ℝ0/ZK_{Y}+\Omega+R\sim_{\mathbb{R}}0/Z and

mld(Y/Z∋z,Ω+R)=ϵ2.\mld(Y/Z\ni z,\Omega+R)=\frac{\epsilon}{2}.

Run an MMP on −KY-K_{Y} over ZZ and let Y′Y^{\prime} be the resulting model with the induced morphism f′:Y′→Zf^{\prime}:Y^{\prime}\to Z. Then −KY′-K_{Y^{\prime}} is nef over ZZ. Moreover, we have

mld(Y′/Z∋z,0)≥mld(Y′/Z,Ω′+R′)=ϵ2,\mld(Y^{\prime}/Z\ni z,0)\geq\mld(Y^{\prime}/Z,\Omega^{\prime}+R^{\prime})=\frac{\epsilon}{2},

where Ω′,R′\Omega^{\prime},R^{\prime} are the pushdowns of Ω,R\Omega,R to Y′Y^{\prime}. Shrinking ZZ to an affine toric neighbourhood of zz, we can apply Lemma 8.2 (by taking X=Y′X=Y^{\prime} and B=0B=0) to deduce that, there are a positive number uu depending on d,ϵd,\epsilon and an effective Cartier divisor FF on ZZ such that z∈Supp⁡Fz\in\Supp F and (Y′,u⋅f′⁣∗​F)(Y^{\prime},u\cdot f^{\prime*}F) is lc over zz. Then (Y,u⋅π∗​f∗​F)(Y,u\cdot\pi^{*}f^{*}F) is lc over zz, as Y⇢Y′Y\dashrightarrow Y^{\prime} is an MMP on −KY-K_{Y}. Thus

μT​(π∗​f∗​𝔪z)≤μT​(π∗​f∗​F)≤1u,\mu_{T}(\pi^{*}f^{*}\mathfrak{m}_{z})\leq\mu_{T}(\pi^{*}f^{*}F)\leq\frac{1}{u},

where uu only depends on d,ϵd,\epsilon. ∎

Proof of Theorem 1.11.

It follows from Theorem 8.3 directly. ∎

Proof of Corollary 1.12.

It is a special case of Theorem 1.11. ∎

9. Exceptional singularities

In this section we will treat the case for exceptional singularities.

Theorem 9.1.

Let ss be a natural number and ϵ,δ\epsilon,\delta be positive real numbers. Then there is a positive real number tt depending only on s,ϵ,δs,\epsilon,\delta satisfying the following. Assume

  • •

    (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) is a klt germ of dimension ss,

  • •

    π:Y→Z\pi:Y\to Z is a plt blow-up of (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) with the exceptional divisor EE,

  • •

    a⁡(E,Z,Δ)≥ϵa(E,Z,\Delta)\geq\epsilon,

  • •

    there is a boundary Ω\Omega on ZZ such that (Z∋z,Ω)(Z\ni z,\Omega) is a klt germ and π:Y→Z\pi:Y\to Z is a δ\delta-plt blow-up of (Z∋z,Ω)(Z\ni z,\Omega).

Then there exists an effective Cartier divisor HH on a neighbourhood of z∈Zz\in Z such that z∈Supp⁡Hz\in\Supp H and (Z,Δ+t​H)(Z,\Delta+tH) is lc near zz.

Proof.

Shrinking ZZ around zz, we can assume that (Z,Ω)(Z,\Omega) is klt everywhere. Applying Lemma 4.5 (by taking X=ZX=Z and B=ΩB=\Omega), we may suppose that ZZ is projective and (Z,Ω)(Z,\Omega) is still klt everywhere. By assumption, we have

  • •

    −E-E is ample over ZZ,

  • •

    a⁡(E,Z,Δ)≥ϵa(E,Z,\Delta)\geq\epsilon,

  • •

    (Y,ΔY+E)(Y,\Delta_{Y}+E) is plt near EE, where ΔY\Delta_{Y} is the birational transform of Δ\Delta, and

  • •

    (Y,ΩY+E)(Y,\Omega_{Y}+E) is δ\delta-plt, where ΩY\Omega_{Y} is the birational transform of Ω\Omega.

Then −(KY+ΩY+E)-(K_{Y}+\Omega_{Y}+E) is ample over ZZ. Let C=ΩY+(1−a)​EC=\Omega_{Y}+(1-a)E where aa is a sufficiently small positive number. Then (Y,C)(Y,C) is a klt pair and −(KY+C)-(K_{Y}+C) is ample over ZZ.

By [HLS19, Proposition 4.4 and Theorem A.1], there exists a natural number n1n_{1} depending on s,ϵ,δs,\epsilon,\delta such that n1​En_{1}E is Cartier. Let AA be a very ample divisor on ZZ such that π∗​A−n1​E\pi^{*}A-n_{1}E, π∗​A−(KY+C)\pi^{*}A-(K_{Y}+C) are ample. Then

(2​π∗​A−n1​E)−(KY+C)(2\pi^{*}A-n_{1}E)-(K_{Y}+C)

is ample. By the effective base point freeness [Ko93], there exists a bounded n2∈ℕn_{2}\in\mathbb{N} depending on ss such that 2​n2​π∗​A−n1​n2​E2n_{2}\pi^{*}A-n_{1}n_{2}E is base point free. Proof of Theorem 1.15.

When Z=1Z=1, Conjecture 1.4 holds obviously. So we may suppose that dimZ≥2\dim Z\geq 2. By Lemma 2.27, (Z∋z,Δ)(Z\ni z,\Delta) has a plt blow-up π:Y→Z\pi:Y\to Z. Then π:Y→Z\pi:Y\to Z is also a plt blow-up of (Z∋z,Ω)(Z\ni z,\Omega) since Ω≤Δ\Omega\leq\Delta. By Lemma 2.30, π:Y→Z\pi:Y\to Z is a δ\delta-plt blow-up of (Z∋z,Ω)(Z\ni z,\Omega), where δ\delta only depends on s,𝔇s,\mathfrak{D}. Thus the theorem follows from Theorem 9.1. ∎

The corollary follows from the argument in the proofs of Theorem 4.4 and 4.6, by replacing the assumption that Conjecture 1.3 holds when dimZ≤ℓ\dim Z\leq\ell with Corollary 1.8 and 1.16. ∎

Appendix A Fundamental cycles of quotient surface singularities

We call Z∋zZ\ni z a quotient surface singularity if (Z∋z)=(ℂ2∋0)/G(Z\ni z)=(\mathbb{C}^{2}\ni 0)/G for some finite subgroup G⊂G​L​(2,ℂ)G\subset GL(2,\mathbb{C}). In this appendix, we will show the following proposition.

Proposition A.1.

Let Z∋zZ\ni z be a quotient surface singularity and let π:Y→Z\pi:Y\to Z be the minimal resolution with the exceptional divisor EE. Denote by CfC_{f} the fundamental cycle of Z∋zZ\ni z on YY. Then Cf≤6​EC_{f}\leq 6E.

Lemma A.2.

Let Z∋zZ\ni z and Z′∋z′Z^{\prime}\ni z^{\prime} be two surface singularities. Let Y→ZY\to Z and Y′→Z′Y^{\prime}\to Z^{\prime} be the minimal resolutions with the exceptional divisors E=∑iEiE=\sum_{i}E_{i} over Z∋zZ\ni z and E′=∑iEi′E^{\prime}=\sum_{i}E^{\prime}_{i} over Z′∋z′Z^{\prime}\ni z^{\prime} respectively. Assume that

  • •

    the number of components of EE is the same as that of E′E^{\prime}, and

  • •

    Ei⋅Ej≥Ei′⋅Ej′E_{i}\cdot E_{j}\geq E^{\prime}_{i}\cdot E^{\prime}_{j} for any i,ji,j.

Let Cf=∑ici​EiC_{f}=\sum_{i}c_{i}E_{i} and Cf′=∑ici′​Ei′C^{\prime}_{f}=\sum_{i}c^{\prime}_{i}E^{\prime}_{i} be the fundamental cycles on YY and Y′Y^{\prime} respectively. Then ci≥ci′c_{i}\geq c^{\prime}_{i} for any ii.

Proof.

Denote C~f=∑ici​Ei′\widetilde{C}_{f}=\sum_{i}c_{i}E^{\prime}_{i}. For any component Ek′E^{\prime}_{k} of E′E^{\prime} we have

C~f⋅Ek′=∑ici​Ei′⋅Ek′≤∑ici​Ei⋅Ek=Cf⋅Ek≤0.\widetilde{C}_{f}\cdot E^{\prime}_{k}=\sum_{i}c_{i}E^{\prime}_{i}\cdot E^{\prime}_{k}\leq\sum_{i}c_{i}E_{i}\cdot E_{k}=C_{f}\cdot E_{k}\leq 0.

By the definition of the fundamental cycle, C~f≥Cf′\widetilde{C}_{f}\geq C^{\prime}_{f}, that is, ci≥ci′c_{i}\geq c^{\prime}_{i} for any ii. ∎

Let Z∋zZ\ni z be a quotient surface singularity and let π:Y→Z\pi:Y\to Z be the minimal resolution with the exceptional divisor EE. By Lemma 2.21, EE is a simple normal crossing divisor on YY. The dual graph Γ\Gamma associated to the minimal resolution of Z∋zZ\ni z is defined as follows.

  • •

    A vertex vv of the Γ\Gamma corresponds to a component EvE_{v} of EE.

  • •

    Two vertices v,wv,w are connected by kk edges if the corresponding components Ev,EwE_{v},E_{w} meet each other in kk points.

  • •

    Each vertex vv is decorated with a weight: the self-intersection number of EvE_{v}.

It is clear that the intersection matrix of components of EE is determined by the dual graph. Hence the fundamental cycle is determined by the dual graph.

A complete list of quotient surface singularities and the dual graphs associated to their minimal resolutions can be found in [BO12, pp.11-16]. Using Laufer’s algorithm (see Remark 2.24), we calculate the fundamental cycle CfC_{f} on the minimal resolution of each singularity in the list and we conclude that Cf≤6​EC_{f}\leq 6E.
